title: Alvah-i-Visaya (Will and Testament)
first_line: All praise to Him Who, by the Shield of His Covenant, hath guarded the Temple of His Cause from the darts of doubtfulness... O God, my God! Shield Thy trusted servants from the evils of self... O Lord by God! Assist Thy loved ones to be firm in Thy Faith
first_line_orig: حمدا لمن صان هیکل امره بدرع المیثاق عن سهام الشبهات و حمی حمی شریعته السمحاء

title: Tadhkiratu'l-Vafa (Memorials of the Faithful)
first_line: There was, in the city of Najaf, among the disciples of the widely known mujtahid
first_line_orig: در نجف اشرف در دائره شیخ مرتضی انصاری مجتهد شهیر شخصی بی نظیر بود

title: Maqaliy-i-Shakhs Sayyah (A Traveller's Narrative)
first_line: Touching the individual known as the Bab and the true nature of this sect diverse tales are on the tongues
first_line_orig: در خصوص شخص معروف بباب و حقیقت احوال اینطائفه روایات مختلفه و تفاصیل

title: Madaniyyih (The Secret of Divine Civilization)
first_line: Praise and thanksgiving be unto Providence that out of all the realities in existence He has chosen the reality of man
first_line_orig: بدایع حمد و ثنا و جوامع شکر و سپاس درگاه احدیت پروردگاریرا سزاست که از بین کافه

title: Lawh-i-Hizar Bayti (Tablet of the Thousand Verses)
first_line: O Lord! Thou beholdest the assault of the nations and their violent commotion, and the pride of the peoples and their fierce onslaught against this lone and solitary servant [3.5s]
first_line_orig: ای رب تری هجوم الامم و جولتها و غرور الملل و صولتها علی عبدک الفرید الوحید

title: Tafsir-i-Kuntu Kanzan Makhfiyyan (Commentary on the Hadith of the Hidden Treasure)
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath stirred up the celestial spheres of being through the movement of divine attraction, and hath caused the oceans of existence to surge [3.5s]... ...And to continue: To him who looks at these lines and understands these indications, it is well known with respect to the request of that traveller… O Lord so rich in bounty, so replete with grace
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی قد حرک افلاک الذوات بحرکه جذب صمدانیه و قد موج ابحر الکینونات

title: Tafsir Ghulibatu'r-Rum (Commentary on the Hadith "Rome was Overthrown")
first_line: Praise be to Thee, O Lord! O my God! Out of Thy Bounty and Mercy, Thou hast caused the waters of existence to descend from the heaven of Thy Oneness
first_line_orig: سبحانک اللهم یا الهی قد نزلت من سماء عز احدیتک میاه الوجود بجودک و رحمانیتک

title: Lawh-i-Hizar Bayti II (Second Tablet of the Thousand Verses)
first_line: O thou who hast devoted thy life to the exaltation of the Word of God! What thou hast written was perused
first_line_orig: یا من وقف حیاته لاعلاء کلمه الله آنچه مرقوم فرموده بودید ملحوظ گردید و بدقت

title: Tafsir-i-Ayat-i-az Suriy-i-Kahf (Commentary on the Surih of the Cave)
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath sent down verses from the Kingdom of grandeur and power, and made them a proof for the people [3.5s]... ...As to the intended meaning of Dhu’l-Qarnayn in this verse, it is none other than Mu?ammad Himself—may the spirits of them that are nigh unto God be a sacrifice for Him
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی نزل الایات من ملکوت العظمه و الاقتدار و جعلها حجه لاهل

title: Lawh-i-Shuhaday-i-Yazd va Isfahan (Tablet on the Martyrs of Yazd and Isfahan)
first_line: In this enlightened age, which is the century of the Almighty God, by the effulgence of the Sun of Reality, the lights of civilization are diffused
first_line_orig: در این عصر انوار که قرن عظیم حضرت پروردگار است و از پرتو شمس حقیقت انوار

title: Siyasiyyih (The Art of Divine Polity - Treatise on Politics)
first_line: Adoration and praise beseem the Spirit of Purity that has laid the foundation of creation with the sole object
first_line_orig: ستایش و نیایش پاک یزدانیرا سزا که بنیان آفرینش را بر ظهورات کمالات مقدسه عالم

title: Tafsir-i-Ayat-i-az Suriy-i-Ra'd (Commentary on the Surih of the Thunder)
first_line: Praise be to God! The tongues of the eloquent ones give utterance to wondrous and comprehensive wellsprings of praise and thanksgiving [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله تنطق السن البلغاء ببدایع جوامع منابع اذکار الحمد و الثناء و مظهر

title: Tafsir-i-Bismillah
first_line: ...The names of God derive from those attributes which are the perfections belonging to the reality of the Essence
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی بفیض ظهوره الاعلی کشف الغطاء عن وجه الهدی و اشرقت الارض

title: Commentary on the Tradition "Heaven and Earth cannot contain me"
first_line: Praise be to God, Who hath bestowed upon His servants grace and bounty in these days wherein He hath manifested [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله بما من علی العباد بالفضل و الافضال فی هذه الایام التی فیها تجلی علی

title: Tafsir-i-Suriy-i-Qalam (Commentary on the Surih of the Pen)
first_line: Praised be to God Who made the Point to be outstretched within the Book of Origination, an Ornament through which is the Genesis of Creativity
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی جعل النقطه البارزه فی کتاب الابداع طراز جداول الاختراع و فصل

title: Lawh-i-Lahih (Tablet to the Hague)
first_line: O ye esteemed ones who are pioneers among the well-wishers of the world
first_line_orig: ای اول اشخاص خیرخواه محترم عالم انسانی نامه های شما که درین مدت حرب ارسال

title: Tafsir-i-Ayat-i-Qayyumu'l-Asma (Commentary on a Verse from the Qayyumu'l-Asma)
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath ordained that the Line, proceeding from the Primal Point manifested in the letter Bá, be the ornament of the seal [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی جعل الخط المتکون من النقطه الاولیه الظاهره بالباء طراز الختم

title: Commentary on the Tradition "Dost thou see a man"
first_line: Praise be unto Him Who, in the essence of His Being, is exalted above all description of contingent things and Who, in the reality of His Nature, is sanctified from every attribute [3.5s]... ...O thou who hast turned thy face towards the court of eternity, and art even as a brand afire with the flames of the Burning Bush! Concerning thy question about the term “angels”… And now concerning thy question about the 'Jinn', know thou that God - exalted be He - hath created man from four elements: fire, air, water and earth
first_line_orig: الحمد لمن تعالی بجوهر ذاته عن وصف الممکنات و تقدس بساذج حقیقته من نعت

title: Chapter 11, Commentary on the Eleventh Chapter of the Revelation of John
first_line: In Revelation 11:1–2 it is said: “And there was given me a reed like unto a rod
first_line_orig: در باب یازدهم آیهء اول از مکاشفات یوحنا میفرماید "و نئی مثل عصا بمن داده شد

title: Lawh-i-Dr Forel (Tablet to Dr Forel)
first_line: O revered personage, lover of truth! Thy letter dated July 28th, 1921, hath been
first_line_orig: ای شخص محترم مفتون حقیقت نامه شما که ۲۸ جولای ۱۹۲۱ مورخ بود رسید مضامین خوشی

title: Tafsir-i-Ayat-i-az Suriy-i-Jinn (Commentary on the Surah of the Jinn)
first_line: Praise be to God, the First without beginning and the Last without end, Who hath created the earth and the heavens and brought forth through His power of creation [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الاول بلا اول و الاخر بلا آخر الذی خلق الارض و السماء و ابدع

title: Lawh-i-Du-Niday-i-Falah va Najah (Two Calls to Success and Prosperity)
first_line: O ye concourse of the Kingdom of Abha! Two calls to success and prosperity are being raised from the heights of the happiness of mankind…
first_line_orig: ای اهل ملکوت ابهی دو ندای فلاح و نجاح از اوج سعادت عالم انسانی بلند است

title: Lawh-i-Aflakiyyih (Tablet of the Celestial Spheres)
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath ever caused His Names and Attributes to penetrate the degrees of existence
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی جعل اسمائه و صفاته لم یزل نافذه احکامها فی مراتب الوجود

title: Lawh-i-'Ahd va Mithaq (Last Tablet to America)
first_line: O ye friends of God! Abdu'l-Baha is day and night thinking of you and mentioning... Consider! The Divine Gardener cuts off the dry or weak branch
first_line_orig: ای یاران الهی عبدالبهاء شب و روز بیاد شما و بذکر شما مشغول زیرا یاران الهی

title: Lawh-i-'Ammih (Tablet to the Aunt)
first_line: O kind aunt! The world hath been stirred into motion by the life-giving breezes of the disposition of thy august Brother
first_line_orig: قد اشرقت الانوار و القوم فی عمه عظیم قد ظهرت الاسرار و الناس فی دهش قدیم

title: Lawh-i-Mahmud Furughi
first_line: O thou who art lost and wandering in the desert! Though thou roamest the wilderness like unto the wind, thou art intoxicated with the wine of divine bounty [3.5s]
first_line_orig: ای گمگشته بادیه پیما اگرچه چون باد بادیه پیماای ولی از جام عنایت سرمست

first_line: O my spiritual loved ones! At a time when an ocean of trials and tribulations was surging up and flinging its waves to the heavens
first_line_orig: ای یاران رحمانی من در حالتیکه دریای امتحان پرموج گشته و موج بلایا باوج رسیده

first_line: Praise be to God Who hath sent down the verses in truth and made them even as a surging and tempestuous ocean casting forth pearls [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی نزل الایات بالحق و جعلها کالبحر المتلاطم المواج تقذف دراری

title: Chapter 9, Baha'u'llah
first_line: Baha'u'llah appeared at a time when Persia was plunged in the darkest ignorance… They consulted together and said, "This man is a magician; perchance he will perform some enchantment"
first_line_orig: اما جمال مبارک در زمانیکه ممالک ایران در چنین ظلمت و نادانی مستغرق

title: Chapter 10, Rational and Traditional Proofs from the Sacred Scriptures
first_line: Today at table let us speak a little of proofs. Had you come to this blessed spot in the days
first_line_orig: امروز در سر این سفره قدری از برهان صحبت بداریم اگر در ایام ظهور نور مبین

title: Tafsir-i-Ayat-i-az Suriy-i-Furqan (Commentary on the Surih of the Criterion)
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath revealed Himself unto the peoples of the contingent world and shed the effulgent lights of His beauty upon all created things [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی تجلی علی اهل الامکان و افاض انوار الجمال لمن فی الاکوان بطراز

title: Tablet of the Divine Plan (U.S. and Canada III)
first_line: O ye apostles of Baha'o'llah - may my life be a ransom to you! The blessed person of the promised One... It behooveth the loved ones of God to be enamoured of one another and to sacrifice themselves... O God, my God! Thou seest how black darkness is enshrouding all regions... O Lord! The ocean of rebellion is surging
first_line_orig: ای حواریون بهاء الله روحی لکم الفداء نفس مبارک موعود در کتاب مقدس رب الجنود

first_line: Thy letter was received, and the doings and ravings of the calumniators described therein have been noted [4o]
first_line_orig: مراسله آنجناب واصل و بر وقوعات و هذیان مفتریان اطلاع حاصل گردید از اینگونه

first_line: O my Lord! I have drawn nigh unto Thee, in the depths of this darksome night, confiding in Thee with the tongue of my heart
first_line_orig: و انی اتقرب الیک یا الهی فی جنح هذه اللیله الظلماء و اناجیک بلسان سری مهتزا

title: Chapter 7, Muhammad
first_line: Now as to Mu?ammad, the people of Europe and America have heard certain tales about the Prophet
first_line_orig: اما حضرت محمد ، اهل اروپا و امریکا بعضی روایات از حضرت رسول شنیده‌اند

title: Chapter 81, Reincarnation
first_line: Our purpose in what we are about to say is to express the truth and not to denigrate the beliefs of others
first_line_orig: آنچه گفته میشود ما را مقصد بیان حقیقت است توهین عقاید ملل دیگر نیست

first_line: Praise be unto Him Whose proof hath shone forth, Whose dominion hath been made manifest, Whose bounties have encompassed all, Whose clear path hath appeared, and Whose Law hath been revealed [3.5s]... ...O God! O God! Thou dost behold me, how my forehead is laid upon the dust of humility and submission and how my face is covered
first_line_orig: حمدا لمن لاح برهانه و ظهر سلطانه و عم احسانه و بانت محجته البیضاء و ظهر شریعته

first_line: O thou who art firm in the Covenant and a champion in the field! Numerous letters from thee were received and their contents were noted... Among them were the tidings concerning the blessed Manifestation in the Book of Daniel [3.5s]
first_line_orig: ای ثابت بر پیمان و مرد میدان مکاتیب متعدده آنجناب واصل و بر کیفیت اطلاع حاصل... از جمله اخبارات بظهور مبارک در کتاب دانیال

first_line: Praise be unto Him Who in His Essence hath sanctified Himself above all likeness to His creatures, and Who through His Attributes hath exalted Himself beyond all similitude to His creation, and is glorified [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حمدا لمن تقدس بذاته عن مشابهه مخلوقاته و تنزه بصفاته عن مماثله مکوناته و تعزز

first_line: O true and loving friend! The effect of the musk-diffusing pen of that faithful companion was even as a sweet fragrance from the mystic rose garden wafting to the senses [3.5s]... ...You have mentioned Mirza Malkam Khan in that he has been enquiring about the conduct and the attitude of these people, although he has full and complete knowledge of the integrity of purpose
first_line_orig: دوست حقیقی مهربان اثر خامه عنبرنثار آن یار وفادار چون نفحه گلشن اسرار مشام

first_line: Glory be unto Thee, O my God! For Thou hast opened the Doors of the Kingdom of Grandeur
first_line_orig: لک الحمد یا الهی بما فتحت ابواب ملکوت العظمه و الجلال علی وجوه احبائک و ظللت

first_line: O thou who hast sacrificed thy spirit and heart, thy being and essence, thy substance and all thou possessest in the path of the resplendent Beauty [3.5s]
first_line_orig: یا من فدی روحه و فواده و ذاته و کینونته و ماله و علیه فی سبیل جمال اشرقت

first_line: O friends! In these days events have come to pass within this prison, and all are from the hidden decrees of God [3.5s]
first_line_orig: ای دوستان در این ایام وقوعاتی در این زندان واقع گشته و جمیع از مقدرات غیبیه

first_line: O Army of God! A letter which was signed by you in general was received... Today in the world of existence, each community is wandering in a wilderness... Be ye kind to the human world and be ye compassionate to the race of man... O Thou Provider! Thou hast breathed over the friends in the West... Well is it with you, as you have followed the Law of God and arisen to observe the Fast during these blessed days
first_line_orig: ای حزب الله نامه ای بامضای شما عموما واصل گردید عبارت در نهایت ملاحت و بلاغت

first_line: Thou art He, O my God, Whose most beauteous names and most sublime likenesses are sanctified above the comprehension
first_line_orig: و انت الذی یا الهی تقدست اسمائک الحسنی و تنزهت امثالک العلیا عن ادراک عقول

title: Shaykh Ahmad and Siyyid Kazim
first_line: Know that in the latter days the Shí‘ahs of Persia had forgotten the truth of the religion of God
first_line_orig: بدانکه شیعیان ایران در اواخر ایام حقیقت شریعت‌الله را فرموش کردند و از اخلاق روحانیان بکلی محجوب

first_line: O Lord, my God, my Best-Beloved, my Aim, my heart’s Desire! This, verily, is the first of the days of Ridvan… In the realm of worship, fasting and obligatory prayer constitute the two mightiest pillars of God’s holy Law
first_line_orig: اللهم یا الهی و محبوبی و مطلوبی و مقصودی ان هذا یوم الاول من الرضوان قد اتی

title: Tablet of the Divine Plan (U.S. and Canada II)
first_line: O ye real Bahais of America! Praise be to His Highness the desired One... O God, my God! Thou seest me enraptured and attracted toward Thy glorious kingdom… The range of your future achievements still remains undisclosed. I fervently hope
first_line_orig: ای بهائیان حقیقی امریک شکر حضرت مقصود را که موفق ...از راحت و آسایش جسمانی و تن‌پروری ...انسان بجهت زندگانی این حیات دنیا خلق نشده است

first_line: O ye dear friends of ‘Abdu’l-Baha! After his visit to the Sacred Threshold, and the Centre round which circle in adoration the Concourse on high, Jinab-i-Farúqí came to stay with ‘Abdu’l-Baha
first_line_orig: ای یاران عزیز عبدالبهاء جناب فاروقی بعد از زیارت بعتبه مقدسه و طواف مطاف ملا

first_line: My God, my God! Thou seest me immersed in the depths of tribulation, submerged in seas of hardship and distress, a target for arrows, pierced and wounded [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الهی الهی ترانی خائضا فی غمار البلاء و غریقا فی بحار الباساء و الضرآء هدفا للنبال مطعونا...  در خصوص آقا میرزا بدیع‌اللّه مختصری بآنجناب مرقوم گردید

first_line: O servant of the one true God! In cycles gone by, although the signs of God’s power and the truth of His Cause were clear and manifest, yet to outward seeming the divine tests were severe
first_line_orig: ای بنده حق در دورهای سابق آثار قدرت الهیه و حقیت امر هر چند واضح و باهر بود

title: Paper presented to the Universal Races Congress
first_line: When travelling about the world we observe an air of prosperity in any country
first_line_orig: ای اهل عالم چون در جمیع عالم سیر و سیاحت نمااید آنچه معمور است از آثار الفت

first_line: O my Lord, my Lord! Sanctified is Thine Essence above the comprehension of minds and understandings, and exalted is Thine Identity above all conjecture and fancy [3.5s]
first_line_orig: مولای مولای تقدس ذاتک عن درک العقول و الافهام و تنزهت هویتک عن الظنون

first_line: Glory be unto Thee, O Thou whose mercy hath encompassed all things, whose gift is made perfect, whose power hath encircled the world… Ye who are the sincere well-wishers of the state, who are the dutiful and compliant subjects of the government
first_line_orig: اللهم یا من سبقت رحمته و کملت نعمته و احاطت قدرته و تمت حجته و ظهرت ایاته

first_line: O ye the cherished loved ones of Abdu'l-Baha! It is a long time now since my inward ear hath heard any sweet melodies out of certain regions
first_line_orig: ای یاران عزیز عبدالبهاء چندیست که از بعضی بلاد یک آهنگ دلربا بگوش جان نرسیده

title: Chapter 48, The Difference between Man and Animal
first_line: We have already had one or two conversations on the subject of the spirit but they were not written down.
first_line_orig: یکدو مرتبه در مسئلهء روح صحبت شد اما نوشته نشد

first_line: I commune with Thee, O my God, at daybreak and eventide, in the bright noontide and the dark of night, and I call upon Thee with my tongue and my heart [3.5s]
first_line_orig: اناجیک یا الهی فی غدوی و آصالی و بهره نهاری و جنح اللیالی و ادعوک بلسانی و جنانی

first_line: There is many a divine wisdom in fasting. Among them is this: that, in the days… O Divine Providence! As I am abstaining from bodily desires
first_line_orig: حکمت الهیه در صیام بسیار است از جمله چون در آن ایام مطلع شمس حقیقت

first_line: O one who is firm in the Covenant! Your letter has arrived. Its contents are very strange, for these doubts are not newly widespread… As to the differences among human beings
first_line_orig: ای ثابت بر پیمان نامه شما رسید مضمون بسیار عجیب زیرا این شبهات تازه اشتهار

title: Chapter 13, Commentary on the Twelfth Chapter of the Revelation of John
first_line: We have explained before that what the sacred scriptures most often mean by the Holy City
first_line_orig: از پیش گذشت که مراد از شهر مقدس و اورشلیم الهی در کتب مقدسه

title: Chapter 82, The Unity of Existence
first_line: Know that the idea of the unity of existence is ancient and is not restricted to the Theosophists and the Sufis alone.
first_line_orig: بدانکه این مسألهٴ وحدة الوجود قدیم است تخصیص بثیاسفه و صوفیه ندارد

title: Chapter 84, The Station of Actions Performed without the Knowledge of God
first_line: Know that such ways, words and deeds are to be lauded and approved, and they redound to the glory of the human world.
first_line_orig: بدان که این اعمال و رفتار و گفتار ممدوح است و مقبول و شرف عالم انسانیست

first_line: My God, my God! I cannot reckon my praise unto Thee. How can I recount Thy praise when the minds of them that are endued with understanding are astounded? [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الهی الهی لا احصی ثناء علیک و کیف احصی الثناء و قد ذهلت عقول اولی العرفان عن

first_line: Praise be to Him Who hath rent the dark asunder, hath blotted out the night, hath drawn aside the coverings and torn away the veils... O my Lord and my Hope! Help Thou Thy loved ones to be steadfast in Thy mighty Covenant... O God, my God! Praise be unto Thee for kindling the fire of divine love... Exert every effort in the fields of development and of civilization
first_line_orig: الحمد لله الذی کشف الظلام و محی الغمام و کشف الحجاب و ازال النقاب فلاحت

first_line: O ye who are attracted toward the Kingdom and have drunk the Wine, the nature of which is cool and exhilarating! In these days that the Bestowals of the Kingdom of Abha

first_line: Didst thou not hear that I went to America? France in comparison to America is very near...

title: Public address given on 1912-Apr-16

first_line_orig: انسان باید همیشه شعله را بنشاند.  چون که این عالم همه اش شعله است، عالم نزاع و جدال است.  نزاع میانه

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken at True home on 1912-Nov-02
first_line: The first duty of the members is to effect their own unity and harmony, in order to
first_line_orig: اول وظیفه اعضا الفت و اتحاد آنهاست که سبب حصول نتائج حسنه گردد

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-22
first_line: In these days the most important affair is to render a worthy service at the Holy Divine Threshold and this is no other but the guidance of the people of the earth.

title: Words to the friends, spoken at Hotel Marquardt on 1913-Apr-30
first_line: Consider what wonderful love is this that has been established between us through the power of His Holiness Baha'u'llah! The Shah of Persia came twice to Stuttgart.
first_line_orig: این چه محبتی است که بقوهٴ حضرت بهآءالله در میان ما احداث شده پادشاه ایران دو مرتبه

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: You must be thrilled that on such a Day you have come to the Holy Land.... This is an explicit promise and clearly enunciated by the Divine Prophets. They have foretold that even outwardly, the Jews will come to the Holy Land and once more reclaim their ancient splendor.
first_line_orig: باید بسیار مسرور باشید که در چنین روزی بارض مقدس رجوع نمودید واقعا از تدین و صفای طینت

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-08 in Paris
first_line: You must act on the divine counsels, inasmuch as they are the remedy for every ailment. Make use of this cure. Be mindful of God. Have discussions on spiritual subjects
first_line_orig: باید بوصایای الهیه عامل شوید زیرا این وصایا علاج هر دردی است این علاج را بکار برید

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: The Egyptian chiefs want to become Wahabbi and promote Wahabbi convictions. Perchance they hope to resist European expansion through wars, violence, confrontations and slaughter.
first_line_orig: بزرگان مصر میخواهند وهابی بشوند عقاید وهابیان را پیش گیرند شاید بحرب و ضرب و جنگ

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken on 1912-Aug-03
first_line: The explanations must be adapted to the capacity of the hearers and suited to the exigency of the time.
first_line_orig: بیان باید بمشرب حضار و اقتضای وقت باشد حسن عبارات و اعتدال در ادای معانی و کلام است

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken en route in train on 1912-Sep-30
first_line: Peter was devoid of all schooling and so untrained that he could not remember the days of the week. He would tie up seven loaves of bread and open one each day.
first_line_orig: پطرس از تربیت ظاهری مقدس و مبری بود بدرجه ئی که ایام هفته را نمیتوانست نگاهدارد هفت بستهٴ نان می بست

title: Words to the Portland and Seattle Baha'is, spoken at Goodall home on 1912-Oct-22
first_line: Until now it never happened that someone from the East, impelled by the promptings of his conscience, should come to the West to see the friends of God... A great war and commotion shall inevitably take place
first_line_orig: تا حال واقع نشده که از شرق شخصی بغرب بیابد محض انبعاثات وجدانی و ملاقات دوستان الهی

title: Words spoken on 1915-Aug-03 in Haifa
first_line: Now when the world is in tumult and confusion, We shall behold what shall come to pass after this tempest; God willing, it shall be well [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حالا که عالم مغشوش است تا ببینیم بعد از این طوفان چه می شود، انشاء الله خوب می شود.  این دول بدون اینکه مشکلات

title: Words spoken ca. Feb. 1920
first_line: The acquisition of confirmations is dependent on teaching the Cause. If the teaching is stopped, then confirmations will likewise cease… It is incumbent on each and every one of the believers to lead, in the span of a year, at least one person to the river of guidance
first_line_orig: حصول تائید منوط بتبلیغ است اگر تبلیغ تعطیل شود تائید نیز منقطع خواهد شد . تائید معلق و موکول به قیام است

title: Words spoken on 1916-May-30 in Haifa
first_line: The Exalted One declareth: Howsoever loftily the people of ascent may soar unto the heights of divine knowledge, in the end must they return unto their own selves [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حضرت اعلی می فرماید که هر قدر اهل عروج به معارج عرفان صعود کنند بالأخره راجع می شوند به انفس خود

title: Words spoken on 1915-Aug-08 in Haifa
first_line: He saith: These verses are revealed from Mine own nature, not from Gabriel. Ever was it a spiritual communion, an unceasing communication [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حضرت می فرمایند این آیات از فطرت من نازل می شود، از جبرئیل نیست.  همیشه مخابرهٴ معنوی بود، مخابرهٴ مستمره بود

title: Words to some Baha'is, spoken at Plaza Hotel on 1912-Apr-29
first_line: You have a good city. The call of God was first raised in this city. I hope that in Chicago the Cause of God will progress greatly... The severest tests were in Persia.... This building commands a good view
first_line_orig: خوب شهری دارید ندای آلهی اول در این شهر بلند شد امیدوارم که در شیکاغو امر الله نهایت نفوذ حاصل نماید

title: Words spoken on 1915-Sep-08 in Haifa
first_line: Verily, multitudes of men are encompassed by tribulation. The light of faith doth not shine forth that it might become the cause of patience and forbearance. When the heart of man is assured through faith [3.5s]
first_line_orig: خیلی مردم در مخمصه هستند.  نور ایمان هم که نیست تا سبب صبر و تحمل شود.  انسان وقتی که قلبش مطمئن به ایمان است

first_line: In this Dispensation the veil hath grown more impenetrable than in former times. During the Islamic Dispensation the veil had become such [3.5s]
first_line_orig: در این دور حجاب محکمتر از سابق میباشد در دوره اسلام حجاب چنان شده بود

title: Words to Tirandaz, spoken on 1914-Oct-29
first_line: Is this wee bit of an animal your donkey? Your name has just brought to my mind a story of my childhood. At the time of our arrival in Bagdad
first_line_orig: در بغداد کارپرداز ایران بقدری عداوت داشت که وقتی که ذکر جمال مبارک می شد چشمهایش تغییر می کرد.  من طفل بودم از من پرسید تیر می اندازی

title: Words spoken on 1913-Mar-16 in Paris
first_line: During the reign of Mu'awiyah, the caliph, there was an Israelite who claimed to be a Muslim.
first_line_orig: در زمان معاویه شخصی از خاندان اسرائلیان بود

title: Words to a Sufi, spoken en route to Chicago on 1912-Oct-30
first_line: Yes, this is true, but one man is so exalted that others bow down before Him and He is adored by them like Christ or Moses
first_line_orig: صحیح است ولی یک آدمی انقدر عزیز است که مسجود امم میشود مانند حضرت مسیح و موسی داعی بوحدانیت الهیه و سبب تربیت ملتی می گردد

title: Words to pilgrims, spoken on 1914-Jun-10
first_line: The Supreme Báb was the promised one of the Koran. with regard to the question of the Seal of the Prophets

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: ‘Alaviyyih Khanum, the wife of the martyred Mulla ‘Alí Jan [Mafuzaki], had a dream which she recounted to Jamal Burújirdí. She said, “I dreamt that Jamal Mubarak came to this room and graciously spoke in praise of me.”
first_line_orig: علویه خانم عیال ملا علی جان شهید خوابی دیده بود و برای جمال بروجردی نقل کرده بود

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1915-May-08
first_line: Poverty has become widespread amongst all the inhabitants of Syria and our affairs are in such a confused state... the station of such a wealthy man is greater than the poor who is patient
first_line_orig: فقر از هر جهت بر ناس غلبه نموده ما هم امور مان وضعی است که نمیتوانیم

title: Words spoken at Hearst estate in Pleasanton, CA, 1912-Oct-15
first_line: In reality, children are the ornaments at the table... How can we render Thee thanks, O Lord? Thy bounties are endless and our gratitude cannot equal them.... When in the city of Zor the lamp of his life was extinguished
first_line_orig: فی الحقیقه اطفال زینت سفره اند علی الخصوص این اطفال که خیلی ملیحند قلوب اطفال بسیار صاف و ساده است

title: Words spoken on 1914-Feb-08
first_line: The Word of glory and deliverance was sent down upon the children of Israel at a time when all of them had sunk to such depths of abasement [3.5s]
first_line_orig: کلمه عزت و نجات بنی اسرائیل وقتی نازل شد که جمیع انها در ذلت بودند بدرجه

title: Words to Otto Hafner, spoken at Hotel Marquardt  on 1913-Apr-04
first_line: It is good to be a spreader of the Teachings of God in childhood. I was a teacher
first_line_orig: مبلغی در طفولیت خوبست من باین سن که بودم تبلیغ می‌کردم شخصی از احباب برادری داشت

title: Words spoken on 1915-Oct-26 in Bahji
first_line: The purpose of kindling the lamp is not for the shrine itself, but rather for such souls as enter therein, that through this means they may be moved to remembrance; for in truth the shrine itself is sanctified [3.5s]
first_line_orig: مقصد از سوزاندن چراغ نه برای روضه است، بل برای نفوسی که وارد می شوند است که به آن واسطه ذکر کنند والا خود روضه مقدس است

title: Words spoken on board the SS Celtic in port, 1912-Dec-13
first_line: I come from America, where I spent nine months as a traveller. I spoke at many churches and synagogues
first_line_orig: من از امریکا میآیم نه ماه در آن ممالک مسافر بودم در اکثر کنائس و مجامع نطق کردم

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken at 227 Riverside Drive on 1912-Nov-26
first_line: I always derive great pleasure from being with you. I shall always remember these gatherings. I shall never forget them.
first_line_orig: من از ملاقات شماها کمال سرور حاصل مینمایم همیشه این محافل را در خاطر خواهم داشت ابداً فراموش نخواهم نمود

title: Words spoken on 1916-Feb-14 in Haifa
first_line: When in 'Akká seventy souls from among the Orthodox were required by the government to pay the poll-tax, yet, being poor, they remained helpless [3.5s]
first_line_orig: وقتی در عکا هفتاد نفر از ارتودکس ها را حکومت گرفت که جزیه بدهند،  ولی چون فقیر بودند عاجز ماندند

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: One day in Baghdad, I went hunting with two or three of the friends. Riding a camel, an unclad Arab Bedouin came towards us.
first_line_orig: یکروز در بغداد با دو سه نفر از احباب به شکار رفتیم یک عرب برهنه سیاه سوخته سوار شتر بود

title: Words spoken on 1913-Mar-29 in Paris
first_line: Once during the imprisonment of the Blessed Beauty, I was very insistent to be taken to see Him.... They sent me with a black servant to His blessed presence in the prison. The warders indicated the cell
first_line_orig: یکوقتی ما در طهران همه نوع اسباب آسایش و زندگانی داشتیم ولی در یکروز همه را غارت نمودند

title: Words to Myron Phelps and Madame Canavarro in Dec. 1902
first_line: God is to every human being as great as the individual mental capacity permits one to see Him. So, also, is the Manifestation who represents Him in this world of beings.

title: Words to Julia Grundy spoken around Jan. 1905
first_line: These are precious and wonderful days in ‘Akká. Each day is as a year. Your visit cannot be measured merely by the length of time you have been here.

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-28
first_line: A crow was perched on the lofty branch of a tall tree. In its beak it carried a piece of cheese. It so chanced that two jackals passed by under the tree.

title: Words to Charles and Mariam Haney spoken in Feb. 1909
first_line: In Yazd an ordeal transpired unparalleled in history. After the enemies had besieged he quarter inhabited by the believers, they assaulted them

title: Words to Arthur Agnew et al, spoken on 1907-Apr-14
first_line: This kind of food is not Persian. It is European... There is no grape in the Kingdom. This is a symbol or sign of the Word of God. The intoxication of this wine is such that it will be seen.

title: Words to E.J. Rosenberg et al, spoken around Feb. 1901
first_line: All things in creation are composed either of simple atoms or of compound particles. In the mineral kingdom, many substances such as gold are composed of simple atoms... In the case of Prophets, some have the power to sway and subdue one country only

title: Words spoken on 1914-Apr-07
first_line: My God ever assist and confirm you. Whenever you go to visit the Holy Tomb you must implore and supplicate that God may surround you with His invisible confirmations.

title: Words to some Druze friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-03
first_line: I read in a newspaper the other day a story concerning the present conflict raging between the European Powers

title: Words to Kinney, Beede, Thompson party, spoken on 1909-Jul-04
first_line: We cannot in this world realize the bounty of God, nor can we appreciate His Love, but in the next world we can do so.

title: Words to Myron Phelps and Madame Canavarro in Dec. 1902
first_line: The reference of the words of the Old Testament 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth' is double

title: Words to a stranger, spoken on 1914-May-09
first_line: There are two kinds of understanding; objective and subjective... O God! Refresh and gladden my spirit.... Beg everything thou desirest from Baha'o'llah. If thou art asking faith, ask of Him.

title: Words spoken at House of the Master in Haifa, 1914-Jul-23
first_line: Having then realized how these holy, spiritual, luminous Manifestations sacrificed their lives, teaching us with deeds and not words... then if we have one grain of loyalty how can we stand by idle

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-08 in Tiberias
first_line: God willing, ye shall be always under the protection of the Truth. In your behalf, I seek favor and bounty from the Blessed Beauty. Rest ye assured.

title: Words to George Winterburn et al, spoken on 1904-Feb-06
first_line: The existent world needs a uniting power to connect nations. There are various uniting powers in the world. One is patriotism

title: Words to Julia Grundy spoken around Jan. 1905
first_line: In America you have only received a taste of the spiritual food... Concentrate the soul upon God so that it may become as a fountain pouring out the Water

title: Words spoken ca. 1912-Apr-22 in Washington
first_line: In the world of existence there are three stages, the mineral, the vegetable, and the animal.

title: Words spoken on 1912-Jul-21 in New York
first_line: I feel a zephyr blowing from the Supreme Kingdom towards America. It will continue to blow. I hope it brings the utmost strength to the Covenant.

title: Words to Mr Frosell and his brother, spoken at Ritz Hotel on 1913-Apr-11 in Budapest
first_line: I have come here to see men and not piles of stones and clay. These buildings you can find everywhere; for my part I am searching for men.

title: Words to Marie Watson et al around Aug. 1921
first_line: I plant a seed in your mind; if your heart approves it, it will become a tree and bear fruit... When the brain cells in the 'upper chamber' are active, they respond to celestial vibrations... Discerning, conscious souls who comprehend the reality of the divine teachings are few in every age.

title: Words to Julia Grundy spoken around Jan. 1905
first_line: We must love all humanity as the children of God. Even if they kill us we must die with love for them.
Christ was asking of His disciples whom He was, and when Peter answered: 'Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God'... Let me now compare the words of Christ to the lives of the Popes.

title: Words to Siyyid Asadollah around March 1912
first_line: When Jesus Christ was on earth He taught for three years and was then crucified. As he hung on the cross, during those dark hours

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Feb-19
first_line: It so happened that while in Baghdad, during the season that the pilgrims arrived from all over the Islamic world to visit the Holy Shrines

title: Words spoken at House of Abbud in Akka, 1914-Dec-01
first_line: Those persons who are firm in the Faith during these days shine like unto the brilliant sun and are the cause of the tranquility of the hearts; but those whose hearts are not set aglow

title: Words to Baha'is from Portland, Oregon, spoken on 1912-Oct-16
first_line: Alláh-u-Abhá! You are very welcome.... Because I longed to see you, I have shortened my visit to the country, and here am I.

title: Words to Mary Lucas and other pilgrims, spoken on 1905-Feb-02
first_line: These words of Christ were addressed to the Jews and Pharisees. By coming in the name of the Father

title: Words to Remey and Struven on 1910-May-18
first_line: In fact, you have shown forth a wonderful devotion; you left the West and came to the furthermost part of Asia

title: Words to the friends, spoken on 1914-Mar-09
first_line: The good deeds of man are like unto the sweet fragrances emanated from the musk... As his deeds have been performed with no reference to the applause and commendation of men he enjoys them more than any one else.

title: Words to Fugeta et al, spoken on 1920-Jan-01
first_line: The reality of spirit, because it is not corporeal, cannot be in bodily form. We cannot say it is like the fire, or like water.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Sep-02 in Ramleh
first_line: Once there was a theologian who took a sea trip. While he was walking on the deck and watching the calm sea... By these remarks I do not mean that religious study must be entirely neglected

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1915-Apr-03
first_line: These [locusts] are the armies of God. They are countless in number. Look at them how they fly. How high they are ascending in the air. They must also be fed.

title: Words to Mrs. C, Emogene Hoagg et al, spoken on 1920-Oct-24+25
first_line: This is the Lord's supper. Sometimes the material things have a spiritual effect - for instance, music is material but has an effect over the spirit

title: Words spoken in Feb. 1911
first_line: Fasting is a symbol. Fasting signifies abstinence from lust. Physical fasting is a symbol
Now listen unto what I say for it is the foundation of success and the basis of righteousness
The Blessed Beauty of El-Abha (Baha'o'llah) - may the divine souls of the existence be

title: Words to several Baha'is, spoken at 309 W 78th St on 1912-Jul-01
first_line: I desire to make manifest among the friends in America a new light that they may become a new people

title: Words spoken on 1913-Aug-23 in Ramleh
first_line: The stories of the prophets recorded in the Koran are not for the sake of recording history. They are as warnings to future generations after Mohammed
God has given man a heart and the heart must have some attachment

title: Words spoken in Sep. 1911 in London
first_line: God has created the world as one -- the boundaries are marked out by man. God has not divided the lands
Verily the founding of the Mashrak-el-Azkar will mark the inception of the Kingdom of God on earth. It is the manifest Standard waving in the center of that great continent

title: Words to Wilson, Engelhorn, Stewart, Brittingham, spoken around 1909-Oct-23
first_line: Bodily matters are not important. The physical suffering of Christ passed away

title: Words spoken to Miss St. in Aug 1910
first_line: Der Engländer hat ein unerschutterliches Staatsbewußtsein, welches mit seinem Geschäftssinn ganz verwachsen ist; deswegen ist er der geborene Eroberer und Kolonisator

title: Words to Helen Goodall and Ella Cooper spoken in Jan. 1908
first_line: The love shown by animals is instinctive and not dependent upon their own will--that is, they are endowed with their qualities and use them in a natural way

title: Words spoken on 1911-Oct-17 in Paris
first_line: I wish you to study the works of the Blessed Beauty and to live according to His teaching.

title: Address to the Baha'is at 309 W 78th St in New York, 1912-Nov-16
first_line: Wherever the mention of Baha'u'llah rises up, that is the paradise of Abha.
Tell them they should do as they think best in these matters. Should they marry, divorce, leave their homes, move to other places

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-18
first_line: Prayer and supplication are two wings whereby man soars toward the heavenly mansion of the True One.

title: Words spoken ca. 1919
first_line: God treats these people with His mercy, not with His justice, since God is against war.
Until now it has been said that all religions were composed of tenets that had to be accepted, even if they seems contrary to science.

title: Words to the secretary of the New York Peace Society, New York, 1912
first_line: You must rest assured and let there be no trace of doubt in your souls that God is your assister and helper

title: Words to Mirza Asadullah Qumi, spoken around Sept. 1910
first_line: Do you realize the meaning of my statement... Tell the friends, how, under severe circumstances of bodily weakness, I have accepted... A clipping from the newspaper of Moaid...
Such is the way that must be adopted, for only through intimate association.... The Temple of Ishkabad is unique in that it is the first temple of the kind

title: Words spoken on 1912-Oct-11 in San Francisco
first_line: We went for a short drive and walked through the Sutro Gardens, which are very beautiful. San Francisco has capacity - capacity for many things

title: Words spoken on 1912-Oct-19 in Los Angeles
first_line: Welcome! Welcome! Are you all well? Are you all happy? I am very happy to see you all. I have come from a far distant point to see you

title: Words spoken on 1912-Oct-21 in San Francisco
first_line: This morning we were speaking of the fact that God never leaves anything unexplained. He will make everything manifest, even though it may remain hidden for a long time.

title: Words to Mrs Merriman and Mr Reed, spoken at home of Mrs. Marriott on 1912-Oct-08
first_line: It was a day of happiness for me, too. What I discussed this morning was evident as the sun. That was the fundamental oneness of phenomena.

title: Words to Ali-Kuli Khan spoken in 1900
first_line: …every morning when the sun comes up, it does not first send out a herald to wake up the townspeople and tell them to rise and go to work.

title: Words to a troop of actors, spoken on 1912-Dec-21
first_line: All these people thought they were waiting for Christ and that they were His intimate friends

title: Words spoken on 1915-Jul-29 in Haifa
first_line: The area between Haifa and Acre will be developed; it will be filled with buildings
first_line_orig: از عکا تا حیفا همه معمور می شود.  همه اش باغ و بوستان و بنا خواهد شد.  باغهای بسیار خوب می شود

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: Consider the foolishness of the governments of Iran and the Ottoman Empire, how they banished Baha'u'llah from Iran to Baghdad and Istanbul... Perchance it is because of this that Jewish people will embrace the Cause, since there is no other course left to them.
first_line_orig: انظروا جنون دولت ایران و دولت الاتراک کیف نفوا بهاء الله من ایران و بغداد

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: These people study for fifty years to learn the signs of Return, and yet on the Day of the Manifestation, they have remained deprived.
first_line_orig: اینها پنجاه سال است درس میخوانند که بمعلوم پی ببرند باز در یوم ظهور محروم میمانند

title: Words spoken on 1912-Nov-15 in New York
first_line: Man explains things in two ways. One explanation originates from his personal feelings... In Jerusalem every now and then they broadcast a promise
first_line_orig: بیان انسان دو قسم است یکی بیانی است که فقط منبعث از احساسات شخصی و خیال و فهم اوست این برای همه حجت و میزان نیست

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-06 in Paris
first_line: As this dispensation is one of grace, those who perform goodly deeds and possess a righteous character will not be deprived of divine mercy
first_line_orig: چون این ظهور ظهور فضل است لهذا کسانیکه اعمال طیبه و اخلاق حسنه دارند

title: Words to the friends, spoken at Hotel Marquardt on 1913-Apr-29
first_line: It will be very beneficial to the Cause if a tie of correspondence is established between the German and the American Baha'ís. Spiritual correspondence must be continued
first_line_orig: خیلی خوب است بین دوستان آلمان و امریکا مکاتبه شود تا مزید الفت و ارتباط قلوب گردد

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-17 in Port Said
first_line: We had crossed half the globe in the span of twelve hours when we arrived at Los Angeles on this journey. Had we returned by way of China, Japan, and India, we would have made a full trip around the world
first_line_orig: در این سفر چون بلاس انجلز رسیدیم ١٢ ساعت ریاضی نصف کرهٴ ارض را طی نمودیم

title: Words at table to the friends, spoken in Newton home on 1912-Jun-07
first_line: Nothing in the world of existence is greater than such gatherings as these
first_line_orig: در عالم وجود امری اعظم از اینگونه محافل نیست که محض محبت الله انعقاد گشته ملاحظه نمائید

title: Words spoken on 1913-Sep-21 in Ramleh
first_line: How complex is the life of the present age and how much more complex we

title: Words spoken on 1916-Jul-12 in Haifa

first_line: Praise be to God you had a spiritual time in Germany... Paris is the jungle of nature... The German people are religious.

first_line: In the first days of every Prophet, He was the source of the bounties of God to the people, but after a time, the true spirit of his Teachings waned... Our Lord says that in these early days of the faith, it is of the first importance that all believers should have the right qualities

title: Words to Waite, Harrison et al, spoken on 1909-Oct-13
first_line: Once a Bahá'í was mistaken for his friend and arrested... Your hearts must be like mirrors brightly polished

title: Words spoken en route in carriage in Akka, 1915-Apr-17

first_line: The difference between animal and man is this, that the animal cannot comprehend the teachings of God.... The teachings say first to investigate reality

title: Words to the wife of a professor, spoken at 97 Cadogan Gardens on 1913-Jan-19
first_line: You must thank God that, although I am a person from the East and you are a revered lady from the West, yet we are gathered in this place with the utmost of spiritual affection.

...multitudiness, they all emanate from the solar center. May we be like these trees

Blessed is the soul which is purified, and understands its wickedness and piety.

title: Words to Mr and Mrs Scott, spoken at Baltimore Hotel on 1913-May-07
first_line: You are the flowers of Paris and the cause of my happiness. All the inhabitants of this city are either thinking of industry or wealth or they are chasing after the worldly pleasures

title: Words to the Eastern pilgrims, spoken on 1913-Jun-30
first_line: We must let loose the divine forces so that those souls who are standing still at the turnpike may move along the path of progress... We must ever strive to find out the subject which is of interest to the other party and speak with him from that standpoint.

first_line: The future of the Cause in Germany is very bright. Likewise Budapest and Vienna will become Bahá'í Centers.

title: Words to Ahmad Sohrab, spoken on 1915-Feb-15

title: Words spoken at Haifa Pilgrim House, 1920-Nov-06
first_line: I have been for a walk. Motion is the sign of life. If there be no wind, no motion, the air become impure... our sun with all its planets are moving around a central sun like the moon moves round the earth.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-26 in Ramleh
first_line: There are some people who make this short span of life miserable to themselves and others because they harbor envy in their hearts

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1915-Feb-15
first_line: During our stay in Baghdad there lived in that city one of the Ameers of Afghanistan. He was reputed to be very wealthy and cultured. He used to frequent our house

first_line: The more we thank Bahá'u'lláh for these bounties with which He has encircled us, the more numerous will they become. When Bahá'u'lláh in the early history of the Caused desired to test any one

title: Words spoken at Baltimore Hotel in Paris, 1913-May-11
first_line: There are three paths through which man attains spiritual happiness. The first path is the path of ordeals, trials and difficulties.

title: Words to Dr. Woodsen Allen, spoken at Golden Gate Park on 1912-Oct-10
first_line: Because whatsoever a man soweth here he reapeth there. This world is like a school. He must learn lessons here

title: Words to Alice Beede et al, spoken on 1911-Oct-15
first_line: I am very glad to be here with you. I am very glad to see you all here.

title: Words spoken at Shrine of the Bab, 1920-Jan-04
first_line: In this gathering, all the friends are assembled together in the utmost freedom, happiness and majesty.

The sun of truth rises in each season from a different point of the horizon... People think religion is confined to an edifice, to be worshipped at an altar... This movement eludes organization... There are many people who have never heard of this Revelation that teach its laws and spiritual truths

title: Words spoken in 1912 in the United States
first_line: If a child is left to its own natural proclivities, without education, it will embody all human defects
I have been asked this question: In the Gospels one finds only spiritual directions, not particular directions for conduct as in the old testament.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jul-02 in Port Said
first_line: It is not my duty to command particular persons to arise and teach the Cause

title: Words spoken on 1911-Nov-15 in Paris
first_line: The Laws of God are not imposition of will, or of power, or pleasure, but the resolutions of truth, reason and justice.' All men are equal before the law, which must reign absolutely

title: Words to Remey, Latimer, et al, spoken on 1914-Oct-16
first_line: There was a man by the name of Haji Mohammad Taki Shirazi, who had joined our company.

title: Words spoken ca. 1900
first_line: He who knows nothing of the wind, when he sees trees shaken does not know it is the wind which causes them to shake.

title: Words to Miss Ollie Gish, spoken at 1815 California Street on 1912-Oct-07
first_line: Good morning. Your whistling is wonderful, just like a bird. I have heard the songs of various birds

title: Words to Percy Grant, spoken around 1912-Jul-12
first_line: When one prays, one sometimes has divine glimpses. So, when one is spiritually developed, a sublimity of nature is obtained, a delicacy of vision
In 'Akka [I] was visited by a Christian who expressed his disbelief in dreams.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-26 in Paris
first_line: The Will of God is that these ideals should be promoted. It is certain that anyone who arises to promote them shall be aided

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-28 in Ramleh
first_line: If you are sincere in your love for me, then love and serve the believers of God, then love and serve your fellow-men.

title: Words to Nuru'd-Din Mumtazi et al in May 1920

title: Words to an American, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Mar-27

It [reincarnation] is not as people have understood. What is intended is the return of pre-existent attributes and perfections in new forms.
first_line_orig: این امر مصدق جمیع کتب و مظاهر الهیه است و تعالیم آسمانی دارای دو قسم از احکامست

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Oct-28
first_line: In the time of the Blessed Beauty the kitchen was in the opposite corner and as the hole of the chimney was torturous, the house was always filled with smoke. This high ceiling was black with soot.

title: Words spoken on 1916-May-09 in Haifa
first_line: This is the station of outpouring, and it is the propagation of the Cause of God, the diffusion of the fragrances of God, the exaltation of the Word of God, and the promotion of His teachings. This floweth from the Truth unto creation [3.5s]
first_line_orig: این مقامی است مقام افاضه و آن تبلیغ امرالله و نشر نفحات الله و اعلاء کلمة الله و ترویج تعالیم است.  این من الحق الی الخلق است

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-11

first_line_orig: معلم نمی تواند کامل بکند.  معلم نمی تواند شمع عالم انسانی بکند.  البته طفلی که تربیت نشده باشد ولو بتواند بخواند بهتر از نفسی است

first_line: Readiness is necessary in order to be a recipient of divine bounty. Souls who are prepared are like candles

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907

title: Words to someone who asked for money, spoken at Rue Lauriston 97 on 1913-May-31
first_line: Never be a spendthrift. Do not be extravagant in thy expenses. An extravagant person comes always to a sad end and feels the pinch of want and misery.
first_line_orig: ولی وِل خرجی مکن زیرا اسراف همیشه انسان را ملول و سرگردان نماید من اگر می‌بینید بعضی تعارفات

title: Words to some Theosophists, spoken at Grand Hotel on 1913-Apr-20
first_line: I was most pleased to present myself in your midst and speak with you; a meeting which believes in the spiritual power

title: Words to some Persian Baha'is, spoken on 1913-Oct-23
first_line: We summon the people to severance and enkindlement. We call their attention to spirituality. We have nothing to do with political tricks and chicaneries.

title: Words to Breakwell, Hopper, Brittingham, spoken around 1901-Sep-04
first_line: Everything save man has one condition, but man has two.... One will lift him up, but the other will send him to the lowest depths.

title: Words to E.J. Rosenberg et al, spoken around Feb. 1901
first_line: Good people are of two kinds - those who are so by natural goodness of heart, and those who attain to it by an after gift of the Spirit.

title: Words to Latimer and Remey, spoken on 1914-Oct-14
first_line: The best method is to bury the body. Just as systematically as the body has grown into its present form, it has to be disintegrated.

title: Words spoken en route in carriage in Budapest, 1913-Apr-13
first_line: For nine years He [Bahá'u'lláh] did not see a green leaf. He loved nature. His sensibilities and powers of observation were miraculous. The tips of His fingers were the most sensitive parts of His holy temple.

title: Words to Mr Herrigel, spoken at Grand Hotel on 1913-Apr-20
first_line: The city of Vienna will become a center for the Cause of God: only after my departure the friends must not remain inactive. They must work with greater zeal
first_line_orig: شماها باید از استتکارت باین حدود بیائید و بنشر نفحات اللّٰه بپردازید

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken at Baltimore Hotel on 1913-May-11
first_line: If you have the perceptive power, as soon as you look in the faces of the people, you can observe what ideals are reigning in their hearts.

title: Words to some pilgrims, spoken on 1913-Jun-21
first_line: When Bahá'u'lláh left Baghdad and without the knowledge of the friends went to Suleymaniyyih, one day He met a boy in the street weeping.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Nov-09 in Port Said
first_line: These old veterans of the Cause have been with Bahá'u'lláh in Baghdad, Constantinople, Adrianople and Acca.

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-02 in Tiberias
first_line: His Holiness the Blessed Perfection has raised the station of woman and hath glorified her before the eyes of all the world.

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-13
first_line: Napoleon the great conquered Germany and brought under his control its domain but to what result! It was only a temporary victory.

title: Words spoken on 1915-Apr-17 in Abu Sinan
first_line: Mankind are naturally heedless and prone to commit injustice and excess. They do not turn their faces toward God and do not let their hearts be swayed by ideal emotions. Like unto the beasts they wallow in the mire of materialism

title: Words to Latimer, Esslemont, Randall et al, spoken on 1919-Nov-25
first_line: The gathering of the friends is very good. In one month's time it will be very fresh and green here. This wilderness is where Bahá'u'lláh has crossed.

title: Words spoken at Pleiades Sylvan Bower, Alhammeh near Tiberias, 1914-May-10
first_line: The first Cause of my happiness is to see your faces radiant with the light of reality and your hearts cleansed and purified with the Water of knowledge. There are two kinds of happiness.

title: Words to a stranger, spoken on 1914-May-09
first_line: My objects are the establishment of the Cause of international arbitration, the promotion of the oneness of the world of humanity, the conformity of religion with science and reason

title: Words spoken at 309 W 78th St in New York, 1912-Jul-19
first_line: This time I want to send you with a new spirit, a new strength, to enlighten California

title: Words to Myron Phelps spoken around Jan. 1909 at the home of Mirza Asadu'llah
first_line: All are connected by the bond of existence. What greater bond is there than this? Furthermore, none of these can continue to exist independently

title: Words to Kathryn Rogers(?) spoken in 1900
first_line: Every element in the creation of God exemplifies the beauty and harmony of living, not for ourselves, but for others... It was not given to every star in the heavens to be the first magnitude

title: Words spoken at Grand Hotel in Vienna, 1913-04-23
first_line: The Cause of Baha'u'llah is incomparable to any other Cause, because it is the Collective Center of this age. This Cause regenerates the souls; everyone receives a new baptism and attains to the station of the new birth.
first_line_orig: و دیگر آنکه امر حضرت بهآءاللّٰه را قیاس بامری ننمائید زیرا این امر جامع جمیع امور است

first_line: The believers of Persia made the greatest self-sacrifice and the trip was made possible. They made large and small contributions

title: Words to Edward Getsinger, spoken on 1913-Nov-11

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Nov-06
first_line: Soon after the ascension of the Blessed Beauty I wrote: Erelong ye shall see the banner of the Covenant Hoisted over the world.... Outwardly the holy Manifestations of God were completely humiliated and despised.
first_line_orig: اوائل صعود مبارک من چنین نوشتم که سوف تری رایة المیثاق تحقق علی الآفاق و همچنین شرق منور نما غرب معطر نما

title: Words spoken on 1913-Apr-10 in Budapest
first_line: Had the Persians and the Ottomans not opposed one another, all these nations would now be under their control. Yet they fell into such grievous heedlessness
first_line_orig: ایرانیان و ترکان اگر با هم مخالفت نمینمودند تا حال جمیع این ممالک در تحت اقتدار

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-29 in London
first_line: This diversity is of two kinds. The first kind of diversity involves innate and temperamental differences, which do not preclude the establishment of unviersal concord
first_line_orig: این اختلاف بر دو قسم است قسمی اختلاف اصلی و خلقی است و آن مانع ظهور اتحاد و الفت عمومی نیست

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-15 in Tiberias
first_line: The Cause appeared in Persia. The blood of so many martyrs was shed in Persia that, unquestionably, signs will appear.

title: Address to the Baha'is at 309 W 78th St in New York, 1912-Jun-04
first_line: Their material civilization resembles a glass of the utmost transparency and purity but divine civilization is like a shining lamp.... Provided they behave moderately, the more people advance
first_line_orig: این مدنیت مادی بمنزلهٴ زجاجی است بسیار شفاف و لطیف تا مدنیت الهیه مانند سراجی است

title: Public address given on 1912-Oct-05
first_line: These countries have reached the apex of material progress. They are like bodies in the utmost health... The people of America have a great capacity for the acquisition of spiritual qualities but they are immersed in material affairs
first_line_orig: این ممالک در مادیات کمال ترقی حاصل نموده مانند هیکلی است که در نهایت صباحت و ملاحت است

title: Words spoken on 1915-Nov-02 in Haifa
first_line: These things are revealed that it may become evident that civilization cannot be achieved save through faith and certitude. It is not possible for man [3.5s]
first_line_orig: اینها برای اینست که معلوم شود که جز به ایمان و ایقان ممکن نیست تمدن حاصل شود.  ممکن نیست از برای انسان

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Nov-11
first_line: There were [certain tribes] prior to the time of Moses who numbered among the Arab clans that are no more, that is, no sign of them has remained.
first_line_orig: اینها قبل از موسی بودند از عرب بائده هستند یعنی که خبر شان منقطع شده است

title: Words to a writer of a Beirut daily, spoken on 1914-Mar-16
first_line: The editor of a newspaper or a magazine must ever take the side of Truth. Every fact before its publication must be thoroughly investigated.

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-22 in London
first_line: Following the martyrdom of Jesus Christ, among the services Mary Magdalene rendered was that, by some means or other, she secured a meeting with the emperor of Rome
first_line_orig: بعد از شهادت حضرت مسیح از جمله خدماتش این بود که بواسطه ا‌ی با امپراطور رومان ملاقات نمود

title: Answer to questions, Dublin, 1912-Aug-10
first_line: The basic principles of all religions are the same and the Sun of Truth is one, yet every day it appears from a different dawning point.
first_line_orig: بلی اصول ادیان یکی است و شمس حقیقت واحد ولکن در هر یومی از مطلعی نمودار پس بهآئیان معتقد باصول ادیان و متوجه شمس حقیقتند

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 on 1913-Mar-14
first_line: Religion without prayer is no religion; but in this Movement work and worship must go hand in hand; one must inspire the other.
first_line_orig: بلی در آیات بدیعه نازل که کار و شغل حکم عبادت دارد ولی این دلیل بر آن نیست که عبادات و اذکار

title: Words to the friends, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Apr-06

first_line_orig: بیائید اینمسئلهٴ مهم را بذهن بسپارید شخصی از طهران نوشته که مشیت کلیه همیشه بر عرش ظهور مستویست یعنی همیشه

title: Words spoken on 1915-Oct-23 in Bahji

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-20 in London

title: Words to Mrs Smith, spoken at 309 W 78th St on 1912-Jun-19
first_line: You must always be happy. You must associate with joyous and happy people
first_line_orig: تو یاید همیشه مسرور باشی و با اهل انبساط و سرور محشور و با خلاق رحمانی متخلق

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-02 in Ramleh
first_line: His [al-Afghani's] admirers have written to me that the traces of his tomb are almost effaced, owing to neglect.

title: Words to the Persian friends, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Apr-01

first_line: Sleep did not visit me last night. I sat in contemplation within the garden's enclosure, reflecting upon how God had bestowed such bountiful favor upon us [3.5s]
first_line_orig: دیشب خوابم نبرد.  در غلام گردش نشسته بودم فکر می کردم.  می دیدم که خدا چه موهبتی در حق ما کرده

first_line: It is now demonstrated that all their existent powers have contributed something toward the realization of this world war

first_line: The bounty and power of God is limitless for each human soul. Consider what was the quickening power

first_line: No, for the word generation has a different meaning in different places. Christ referred to the Christ Dispensation, or cycle

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-17 in Haifa
