first_line: Advance always in the Kingdom of Bahá'u'lláh; occupy thy heart always by the mentioning of Bahá'u'lláh

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jul-29 in Ramleh
first_line: Glad tidings of the Kingdom of Abha! We announce to you Glad-tidings of great Joy!... Similar words were spoken almost two thousand years ago.

title: Words spoken ca. Sep. 1911 in London
first_line: We have grown up step by step, always to a state in advance of the last. God's processes are never retrogressive.

title: Words spoken at table on 1914-Oct-30
first_line: Consider how the people bear testimony to the fact that this Religion is universal and its principles are conducive to the welfare of humanity
You must not injure yourselves or commit suicide.... It is not permissible to do to yourselves what Mirza Hassan Afnan did to himself.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-23 in Port Said
first_line: The designation of “son of God” at the time of Moses and Christ was a term which was used also in relation to the Children of Israel
first_line_orig: ابن الله در بودن در عهد حضرت مسیح و موسی اصطلاحی بود که حتی در باره بنی اسرائیل

title: Words spoken on 1914-Feb-16
first_line: In the beginning of the Cause, the friends in Nayreez and Serostan were surging in activity

title: Words spoken at Hotel Marquardt in Stuttgart, 1913-Apr-26
first_line: Speak of our own war, wherein the hosts of aid and confirmation fight against the legions of the darkness of the world of nature
first_line_orig: از حرب خودمان بگوئید که با جنود تأیید و نصرت در مقابل لشکر ظلمات عالم طبیعت

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Sep-17
first_line: I ask the Blessed Beauty to assist you and confirm you. Wherever I go, you will be in my thoughts.
first_line_orig: از عنایت جمال مبارک شما را تائید و توفیق میطلبم در هر جا و محل باشم

title: Words to visitors, spoken at Grand Hotel on 1913-Apr-19
first_line: The Persians, the Austrians, the Germans, the French, the Italian and the English people belong to one common stock of Aryan race…
first_line_orig: از کنار نهر گنگا از هند بایران رفتند و پس از کهرت و تعد و قبائل بعضی رو

title: Words spoken on 1915-Oct-17 in Haifa
first_line: The essence of the Torah was the Ancient Covenant, and that Ancient Covenant was but an allusion to this New Covenant, which is the Covenant of the manifestation of the Lord's revelation in all His attributes and perfection [3.5s]
first_line_orig: اصل تورات عهد قدیم  است و آن عهد قدیم اشاره بود از این عهد جدید که عهد ظهور تجلی رب است به جمیع صفات و کمال

title: Words spoken on 1915-Aug-06 in Haifa
first_line: Friendship doth make easy for man every difficulty. These farmers now, with such hardship, with life so arduous, for them [3.5s]
first_line_orig: الفت از برای انسان هر مشکلی را آسان می کند.  این فلاح ها حال به این مشکلی، زندگانی به این سختی، برای اینها

first_line: The Christ had not sufficient loved ones who would keep watch over His tomb, for His sepulchre was amidst a refuse heap [3.5s]
first_line_orig: المسیح ماکان عنده احباء کفایة بحافظون علی قبره قبره کان فی مزبلة

title: Words spoken on 1919-Dec-25
first_line: Today, inasmuch as it was the Feast of the Nativity of Christ, I proceeded, in accordance with the command of the Beauty, to visit certain Christian friends [3.5s]
first_line_orig: امروز چون عید ولادت حضرت مسیح بود دیدن بعضی دوستان مسیحی رفتم من بموجب امر جمال

title: Words spoken on 1911-Jan-23
first_line: In this Day physical sacrifice hath no value; rather, it is the inner afflictions, hardships and tribulations of the Bahá'ís [3.5s]
first_line_orig: امروز قربانی جسمانی قیمتی ندارد مشکلات و مصائب و بلیات داخلهٴ بهائیان را

title: Words to some American friends, spoken at Baltimore Hotel on 1913-May-24
first_line: America has the capacity of becoming the standard-bearer of international peace. Geographically it is a vast continent, far away from the jealous eyes of the envious neighbors

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-18 in London
first_line: My hope is that you purify your hearts until they resemble this mirror, that they may reflect the light of the perfections and grace
first_line_orig: امیدوارم مانند این آئینه قلوب را صاف و پاک و پاکیزه نمائید تا حکایت از انوار کمالات

title: Words spoken at Rue Lauriston 97 in Paris, 1913-May-30
first_line: One must eat in moderation. Man is not created for food. He must not indulge in eating too much. Overeating is the cause of many diseases.

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jun-12 in Tiberias
first_line: Man must be qualified with the attributes of the Kingdom. Man must characterize himself with the characteristics of the Kingdom.

title: Words spoken on 1915-Sep-19 in Haifa
first_line: This war was greatly prolonged, and concerning the narrative of the fortress, they spoke of Shaykh Tabarsi, saying: "In the fortress of Tabarsi there were one hundred and ten souls." [3.5s]
first_line_orig: این جنگ خیلی طول کشید و بمناسبت حکایت قلعه شیخ طبرسی را فرمودند که:" در قلعهٴ طبرسی صد و ده نفر بودند

title: Words to Miss Boylan, spoken around 1911-Aug-25
first_line: ‘Abdu'l-Bahá said that he had fulfilled that prophecy by building the Tomb of the Báb. He said, "The blessed and holy Tomb (of Baha'u'llah, May my soul be a sacrifice to its dust!) and the Tomb of the Bab on Mount Carmel was the first Mashraq'ul-Azkar…"

title: Words to professors and clergymen, spoken on 1912-Sep-03
first_line: This is the purpose of the people of Baha. Would you not like to serve such an ideal? I hope you will put forth effort in this direction so that the world of men may find real unity
first_line_orig: اینست مقصد اهل بهآء آیا تو نمیخواهی این کار را بکنی تو هم بکوش تا عالم انسانی وحدت حقیقی یابد

title: Words spoken on 1914-Feb-14
first_line: Concerning that which the Blessed Beauty hath uttered regarding the lineage of Israel, that it shall be recorded - this blessed utterance was made at a time [3.5s]
first_line_orig: اینکه جمال مبارک فرمودند سلالهٴ اسرائیل تحریر خواهند شد این بیان مبارک در وقتی بود

title: Words spoken at Hearst estate in Pleasanton, CA, 1912-Oct-14
first_line: What conforms to the divine decree will be realized. In addition, good intentions and sound thoughts attract confirmations.
first_line_orig: آنچه با تقدیرات موافقت نماید تحقق می یابد و علاوه نیت خیر و حسن تدبیر جاذب تأیید است

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-10 in Paris
first_line: Behold what abounding ecstasy the Covenant of the Abha Beauty has kindled within the people, and how it has caused the believers to gather together
first_line_orig: ببینید چه شور و ولوله ای از تأثیر میثاق جمال ابهی در نفوس افتاده

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-21 in Paris
first_line: Some are of the opinion that, by practising asceticism and withdrawing from society, one can rectify one's character
first_line_orig: بعضی بر آنند که بواسطهٴ ریاضت و گوشه نشینی تعدیل اخلاق و تقرب الی الله حاصل میشود

title: Words spoken on 1912-Oct-09 in Palo Alto
first_line: Some called Christ God, some the Word of God, some others the Prophet of God
first_line_orig: بعضی مسیح را خدا بعضی کلمة الله و بعضی نبی الله گفتند و از اینگونه اختلافات

title: Words spoken on 1912-Sep-04 in Montreal
first_line: Yes, the value and greatness of these travels are not known now... At the time of Muhammad's migration to Medina under divine protection, Abu Bakr was with Him.
first_line_orig: بلی قدر و عظمت این سفر هنوز معلوم نیست بعد معلوم می شود چون ما مقصدی از این سفر جز

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-27 in Paris
first_line: When Hajjaj was named chief of the camp, following a period of disorder, he first issued an edict
first_line_orig: بیانات مبارکه از تواریخ زمان اسلام خیلی مفصل بود از آنجمله حکایت حجاج ظالم

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-26 in Paris
first_line: The progress of any things occurs within its own station.  When one considers the mineral, vegetable, animal, and human stations
first_line_orig: ترقی هر شیئی در صقع آن است در مراتب جماد و نبات و حیوان و انسان چون ملاحظه شود

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken on 1912-Jun-23
first_line: The material progress of Europe is approaching its zenith. Everything that reaches its zenith undoubtedly begins to decline.
first_line_orig: ترقیات مادیه اروپا بحد یقف می رسد هر امریکه بحد یقف رسید لابد تدنی نماید

title: Words to two Zoroastrian pilgrims, spoken on 1914-May-31
first_line: It is a mathematical impossibility that a soul may comprehend the purport of the Teachings of Baha-ollah and then arise to oppose them.

title: Words to some students, spoken on 1915-Jun-29
first_line: The teachings of the Blessed Beauty have made the loved ones of God distinguished above all who dwell upon the earth. This is through the blessing of the counsels and teachings of the Blessed Beauty [3.5s]
first_line_orig: تعالیم جمال مبارک نوعی کرده است که احبای الهی از جمیع من علی الأرض ممتازند.  اینها از برکت نصایح و تعالیم جمال مبارک

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-16 in Ramleh
first_line: The future of Germany is very bright. The German people on the whole are religious. They are very noble and progressive. The Cause of God will advance

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-27 in London
first_line: A number of souls, destitute and famished, approached me and begged me to give them something to sustain them
first_line_orig: جمعی فقرای بسیار گرسنه بمن رسیدند و سوال نمودند من آنها را حواله بدکان بقالی کردم

title: Words to Latimer, Remey et al, spoken on 1914-Oct-18
first_line: These people who called on us today were in a state of fright. They are expecting daily
first_line_orig: چقدر اینها مضطربند ابدا سکون ندارند این علامات عدم ایمان است در قران میفرماید

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Jun-23
first_line: These people are following their false imaginings. They say that the letter from the Bab to Yahya begins thus
first_line_orig: چگونه بوهم متمسکند میگویند در اول توقیع حضرت اعلی بیحیی این عبارتست

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-09 in Paris
first_line: Just as the birds and other beasts think, from the break of day, only of seeds and prey, so too is it with these people
first_line_orig: چنانچه طیور و وحوش از صبح بفکر دانه و طعمه‌أند همین طور این مردم متصل در خیال

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: How bitterly cold was that winter! We arrived at a caravansary located by a moat. The journey was full of sufferings and difficulties
first_line_orig: چه زمستان سردی بود و ما در کاروانسرائی وارد شدیم

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Mar-27
first_line: What a great difference exists between men. One person degrades himself to such a degree that he idolizes and worships stones
first_line_orig: چه قدر تفاوتست بین نفوس شخصی چنان خود را پست مینماید که پرستش جماد و اشکال

title: Words spoken in the presence of Zia Baghdadi, ca. 1920
first_line: Concerning the Arab pilgrim in Iraq, the cause of his martyrdom was that some three or four years prior, a family was martyred in that land [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حاجی عرب در عراق سبب ثهادتش این است که سه چهار سال قبل در عراق یک عائله را شهید

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Nov-06
first_line: Baha'u'llah, without earthly power and worldly means, laid the foundations for eternal glory and promoted divine teachings.
first_line_orig: حضرت بهآءالله بدون قواء ملکیه و شئون ظاهره تاسیس عزت ابدیه و ترویج تعالیم الهیه نمود

title: Words to Miss Boylan, spoken around 1911-Aug-25
first_line: Christ healed by the power of his word, because the word of the Messiah was the Holy Spirit

title: Words spoken ca. 1919
first_line: To bathe oneself is a great bounty. Near the army barracks in ‘Akka there existed a public bath which was in a state of ruin
first_line_orig: حمام در حقیقت نعمت بزرگی است در رومیلی در تمام خانهها حمام و آب موجود بود

title: Words to some Greek passengers, spoken en route to Salt Lake City on 1912-Oct-26
first_line: God does not want war. These wars are against the divine will. He desires peace and love for His servants.
first_line_orig: خدا حرب نخواسته این نزاعها مخالف رضای الهیست او بجهت بندگانش صلح و صفا خواسته

title: Words spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Mar-30
first_line: There is a wisdom in this matter which will become known later.
first_line_orig: در این قضیه حکمتی است بعد معلوم خواهد شد

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-16 in Ramleh
first_line: You must give your daughter a Bahai education so that she may become an excellent

title: Words spoken ca. Jan. 1909
first_line: Ye shall align this with the ordinances - far be it from the Divine Power [to withhold it] - yet verily in these are profound meanings [3.5s]
first_line_orig: شما این را تطبیق کنید به قواعد از قدرت الهی بعید نیست ولکن اینها معنی دارد

title: Words spoken on 1915-Sep-11 in Haifa
first_line: Consider ye how these followers of Azal have, until this day, yielded naught but harm and corruption, ruin and upheaval as their fruits for Iran and its people [3.5s]
first_line_orig: شما ملاحظه نمائید که این ازلیها تا بحال جز ضرر و فساد و خرابی و انقلاب چه ثمری از برای ایران و ایرانیان داشتند

title: Words spoken at Rue Lauriston 97 in Paris, 1913-Mar-27
first_line: Fifty years ago Bahá'u'lláh prophesied: 'Adrianople shall go out of the hand of the Sultan' and today that prophecy is fulfilled.... It is evident that negligence from God brings a nation to this path; lack of sound administration

title: Words spoken on 1915-Jul-31 in Haifa
first_line: They razed the holy sites of Karbila and Najaf to the ground, and thereafter did they plough the earth. For nigh upon fourscore years did they till and cultivate that soil [3.5s]
first_line_orig: قتلگاه کربلا و نجف را با خاک یکسان کردند، بعد شخم زدند. قریب هشتاد سال شخم می زدند و زراعت می کردند

title: Words to Mr and Mrs Austin, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Apr-01
first_line: The more the Catholics showed prejudice, the more they were debased. Only now have they shown willingness
first_line_orig: کاتولیکها هر قدر تعصب نمودند ذلیل تر گشتند تا حال که بترتیب جدید راضی شدند و الا این اشخاص متعصب ترین مذاهب عالمند

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: We have nothing to do with the past. “What has passed is past. And what is to come has not appeared. Therefore do not compare two vacuities.”
first_line_orig: ما با گذشته کاری نداریم ما مضی مضی و ما سیاءتیک فاین قم فاغتنم الغرصه بین العدمین

title: Words spoken en route in train in Chicago, 1912-Oct-31
first_line: It is now more than two years that I have been far from the Holy Shrine of Baha'u'llah. Now I must return. If God wills it, I shall make another journey in another direction
first_line_orig: متجاوز از دو سال است که از جوار روضهٴ مبارکه دورم حال باید مراجعت کنم اگر باز مقدر شود

title: Words to a Rabbi, spoken at Emery home on 1912-Dec-04
first_line: What is intended by the creation of heaven and earth in six days is a spiritual creation and a divine day
first_line_orig: مراد از خلق آسمانها و زمینها در شش روز آن روز الهی است و خلق روحانی

title: Words spoken on 1915-Oct-19 in Akka
first_line: The Center of Violation striveth to compass my martyrdom. What shall befall him? This is the utmost aim and desire of mine own self [3.5s]
first_line_orig: مرکز نقض  سعی می کند که سبب شهادت من بشود.  از برای او چه خواهد شد.  این نهایت آمال و آرزوی من است

title: Words to a Unitarian woman on ship, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Mar-26
first_line: The most important of all intentions is to spread the love of God.... Glad tidings, glad tidings, the Sun of love has dawned
first_line_orig: مژده مژده که علم ملکوت بلند شد مژده مژده بهار الهی ظاهر گردید مژده مژده ابر رحمت ببارید

title: Words spoken during filming of motion picture on 1912-Jun-18
first_line: Observe the power of the Ancient Beauty and the influence of the Greatest Name through which He has united us with the people of America in this way
first_line_orig: ملاحظهٴ قدرت جمال قدم و نفوذ اسم اعظم نمائید که ما را با اهل امریکا باین نحو الفت و اتحاد داده

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken at Rue Lauriston 97 on 1913-Mar-25
first_line: I have set a conflagration throughout America. Its results will become known later. Wait for a few years and you will behold the appearance of many traces.

title: Words spoken en route to Salt Lake City, 1912-Oct-27
first_line: I have come to America to raise the standard of universal peace and to promote the unity of mankind. My aim is to create love and harmony among the religions.
first_line_orig: من بامریکا آمدم تا علم صلح عمومی بلند کنم آمده ام ترویج وحدت عالم انسانی نمایم مقصدم الفت و محبت

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-25 in Ramleh
first_line: When I was in America and Europe I went through some of the Zoological gardens... My grandfather had many colored maids and servants. When the Blessed Perfection became the head of the family

title: Words to some Baha'is, spoken en route in automobile on 1912-Oct-03
first_line: No one was a denier of His virtues. All the wise men of the East considered Him the greatest person in the world. But they said, 'Alas, that He has claimed divinity for Himself.'
first_line_orig: نفسی منکر فضائل مبارک نبود و جمیع عقلای شرق اول شخص عالم میدانستند ولی می گفتند حیف که ادعای الوهیت

title: Words to Stanwood Cobb, spoken at Rue Lauriston 97 on 1913-Mar-28
first_line: No. In this movement there will never be any paid ministers, no appointed clergy, no bishops, no cardinals, no popes, no ceremonies.

title: Words spoken ca. Jan. 1909
first_line: Once came hither a certain divine, one of those clerics possessed of pride, at a time when Arabic prayers were being chanted in this place [3.5s]
first_line_orig: یک آخوندی یکوقتی آمد اینجا از آن آخوندهای پر غرور بود اینجا از مناجاتهای عربی تلاوت میشد

title: Words spoken at home of Shaykh Salih in Abu Sinan, 1914-Nov-02
first_line: There was a fanatical Protestant minister that always wanted to argue. One time he came to Me and said, ‘Given His large body and girth, with what kind of ladder did Muhammad ascend to heaven?'
first_line_orig: یک کشیش پروتستان خیلی متعصبی بود همیشه میخواستند مجادله کند یکدفعه آمد پیش من و گفت

title: Words to a newspaper editor, spoken at Hotel Lankershim on 1912-Oct-20
first_line: I will tell you one thing and it will suffice once and for all. Beyond this neither question me nor will I reply. And that is the words of Christ when told that 'your brothers have come to see you.'
first_line_orig: یک کلمه بتو می گویم و این تا آخر کافی است و بیش از ین نه تو سئوال کن و نه من جواب میدهم و آن کلمه بیان حضرت مسیح است

title: Words to E.J. Rosenberg et al, spoken around Feb. 1901
first_line: this means that the death of the body is of no importance and not in the least to be feared... It is said of Mary Magdalen that out of her went seven devils.

title: Words to E.J. Rosenberg et al, spoken around Feb. 1901
first_line: There are two forms of prayer in this religion, that is the obligatory prayers... There is also the form of prayer to which the name 'supplication' has been given

title: Words to Lua Getsinger in 1904
first_line: The baptism of the Christians as practiced today is not the teachings of Christ.

title: Words to Madam J, spoken on 1904-Apr-15
first_line: No, no, one never returns here, for this world is a school where the soul of man learns its first lessons in spirituality

title: Words to Aline Shane-Devin spoken on 1907-Oct-14
first_line: It is as difficult for the human mind to understand the Essence of God as for the watch to understand its maker... The only test of its truth lies in the influence this conception has upon our lives

title: Words to Helen Goodall and Ella Cooper spoken on 1908-Jan-11
first_line: That is very good, that is right for that brings harmony into the meeting. ...the Hidden Words should be read, and often the Tajalleyat

title: Words to Mr and Mrs Hannen, spoken on 1909-Feb-23
first_line: the development of existence may be represented by two arcs forming a circle. The one descending, the other ascending. Beginning with the mineral

title: Words to Mary Hanford Ford et al around 1911-Oct-25
first_line: I am very unhappy to see how wicked and uncivilized human beings can be... See what a slight thing will shut off our physical sight, so will a slight indiscretion, a cross word, an adverse criticism shut off the delicate spiritual sight.

title: Words to Hannen, Latimer et al, spoken on 1912-Aug-01
first_line: All the people of the world are sowing their seeds in brackish ground and they write on the surface of the water. Therefore you must consider that all their efforts are fruitless.

title: Words to the minister of the New Congregational Church, spoken on 1913-Jan-13
first_line: I am only a servant of God. The station of servitude is very great. It is very difficult for any one to live in accord with the requirements of servitude

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-23 in Paris
first_line: The Parisian people are submerged in a sea of materialism. They are intoxicated with the wine of desire and selfish appetites. They think these material objects are permanent.

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Feb-09
first_line: How pitiful it is that man is satisfied with material things and so regulates his life as to gain more and more!

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Feb-16
first_line: How large is the creation of God! How stupendous His machinery! How infinite His dominion!... Were it possible to construct an aeroplane and establish communication between the various planets many marvellous discoveries would have been achieved!

title: Public address given at studio of Mr. Scott on 1913-Feb-17
first_line: This is the work. All else save this has no result. Humanity must become illumined with the light of the Kingdom, otherwise all our efforts will remain fruitless.

title: Words to Mrs. Henlay, spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 on 1913-Feb-18
first_line: Whenever you feel depressed, go alone into the secret chamber, read one of the Hidden Words and with the utmost supplication

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 on 1913-Mar-01
first_line: For the present, in Paris we are all engaged in mentioning the name of the True One. We are all beneath the protection of the Blessed Perfection.

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Mar-15
first_line: There are three ancient Bibles. 1st the Jewish Bible. 2nd the Sanhedrin Bible which was translated by the seventy wisest Rabbis into Greek at the time of Ptolemy. 3rd the Samaritan Bible.

title: Words to Mr Eckstein, spoken at Hotel Marquardt  on 1913-Apr-05
first_line: A thirsty man will run after every fountain, he may drink bitter and stagnant water but at last he will reach to the sweet spring.

title: Words to a woman questioner, spoken at Grand Hotel on 1913-Apr-22
first_line: You must enter in the Kingdom of Abha. In the Kingdom of Abha, there is light upon light. The darkness of sorrow and pain is banished forever

first_line: Any movement that is for the benefit of mankind should be joined by the Bahá'ís. If they are not asked to help, they should offer their services

title: Words to Kinney, Beede, Thompson party, spoken on 1909-Jul-06
first_line: The spiritual food is the principal food, ... the effect of the spiritual food is eternal

title: Words spoken in Sep. 1911 in London
first_line: ...these rappings, etc., were all material things, and of the body. What is needed is to rise above the material

title: Words to Lua Getsinger in home of Juliet Thompson, June 1912
first_line: I appoint you, Lua, the Herald of the Covenant. And I am the Covenant, appointed by Bahá’u’lláh.

title: Words to Albert Vail
first_line: We do not oppose the religion of anyone. We act in accordance with the Gospel. But we must also act
All the believers, both men and women, in the West and in the East, must consider themselves the spreaders
If a person desires to work for the progress of the world of humanity he must turn his face to the Kingdom of Abha

title: Words to a friend of Mrs. Struven
first_line: When ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes tablets, he is calling the souls to a station which they are potentially able to attain. I does not mean that they have attained that station at the time of the writing.

title: Words to Aqay-i-Taqizadeh spoken around Dec. 1911
first_line: In principle, we prefer freedom as it is one of the divine blessings and pleases God. However, this is not because freedom helps with the diffusion and propagation of our Cause, as it is the opposite — namely, our Cause grows better in a repressive environment.

title: Words spoken at the Shrine of the Bab, 1913-Dec-06
first_line: Prostration, according to the explicit text of the Book of God, is confined to the Shrine of the Bab, the Shrine of Baha'u'llah and the Holy House.
first_line_orig: ابداً جائز نیست سجود بجهتی جائز نیست سجود بنص کتاب الله مخصوص مقام اعلی

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-29 in Paris
first_line: The doors are closed on every side, and the way to salvation is barred, unless one is aided with spiritual power
first_line_orig: از جمیع جهات ابواب مسدود است و راه نجات مقطوع مگر بقوهٴ معنویه و تأییدات غیبیه

title: Words spoken at home of Alexander Graham Bell in Washington, 1912-Apr-24
first_line: Yes, most of the great inventions were made in a similar way. For instance, the search for alchemy has brought into being thousands of useful medicines and the desire of finding a direct route to India from Europe became the cause of the discovery of America
first_line_orig: اکثر صنایع مهمه از همین راه اختراع شده مانند طالب کیمیا که سبب ظهور هزارها ادویه مفیده گشته

title: Words spoken at Hotel Schenley in Pittsburgh, 1912-May-07
first_line: If one is fully cognizant of the reason for the incursion of disease and can determine the balance of elements
first_line_orig: اگر مدخل امراض را بدانند و اعتدال عناصر را میزان گیرند در هر عنصری

title: Words spoken on 1914-Nov-24 in Abu Sinan
first_line: If the Covenant-breakers had not frustrated my efforts, I would have assembled some of the Muslim and Christian chiefs
first_line_orig: اگر ناقضین گذاشته بودند من بعضی از روسای اسلام و مسیحی راجمع میکردم

title: Words spoken on board the SS Baron Call at sea, 1913-Dec-03
first_line: If a soul is not severed, if he is not pure and holy, if he is not thoughtful of others.. No one can say he is a Bahá'í.

title: Words spoken on 1913-Aug-10 in Ramleh
first_line: If these Tablets do not stir and move the hearts out of their sleep and do not spur them to insatiable activity, they are harder than stones

Verily, when workers establish partnership with the company in the factory, they shall of their own accord choose souls for consultation, and it is certain that whoso possesseth a greater portion shall have a greater share [3.5s]
first_line_orig: البته کارکنان چون در کارخانه با کمپانی شرکت حاصل نمایند از قبل خود نفوسی برای مشورت انتخاب خواهند کرد و یقین است آنکه مایه بیشتر سهم بیشتر دارد

title: Words spoken in the presence of Zia Baghdadi, ca. 1920
first_line: Man must partake of such fruits as are to be found in the place of his habitation and dwelling [3.5s]
first_line_orig: انسان باید از میوههایی که در محل سکونت و اقامتش موجود است

title: Words to the Master's entourage(?), spoken at Church of the Ascension on 1912-Jun-02
first_line: At the time of my arrival at the church I was in no condition to speak; but when I stood before this great gathering I found the atmosphere of the church filled with the Holy Spirit and so a state of wonderful happiness and joy came over me.
first_line_orig: اول حین ورود بکلیسا حالت صحبت نداشتم اما چون در مقابل آن جمعیت عظیم ایستادم

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken on 1912-Apr-24
first_line: O Baha'u'llah! What hast Thou done? O Baha'u'llah! May my life be sacrificed for Thee!
first_line_orig: ای بهآءالله چه کرده ئی ای بهآءالله بقربانت ای بهآءالله بفدایت ایام را بچه مشقت و بلا گذرانیدی

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-06 in Paris
first_line: this is a new era with unprecedented exigencies… the laws of a former age will not suffice this momentous century… the spiritual laws--which is to say secondary religious laws--must be renewed, and divine truths revitalized
first_line_orig: این عصر عصر دیگر است و اقتضای آن اقتضای دیگر احکام عصر سابق این قرن عظیم را کفایت نکند

title: Words spoken on 1912-12-25 in London
first_line: This is a different matter altogether.  Indeed, reward and punishment constitute the basis of order in this world
first_line_orig: اینمسئلهٴ دیگر است و مجازات و مکافات سبب نظام عالم مثلاً اگر کسی اینجا بیاید
subjects: @murder; causing physical harm, @religion as basis of morality; of divine civilization, @reward and punishment

title: Words spoken at German hostel in Tiberias, 1916-Aug-28
first_line: These souls, whose hearts are bereft of divine mercy, have no recourse but to console themselves through some means; thus do they engage in deeds of wickedness and transgression [3.5s]
first_line_orig: اینها قلبشان از رحمت الهی مأیوس است لابدند که خود را به یک چیزی تسلی دهند،  اینست که به فسق و فجور مشغول می شوند

title: Words to Counsel Schwartz, spoken on 1913-Apr-04
first_line: There will be a general war between the European powers and Germany of course will take a prominent part. Bahá'u'lláh has predicted a war between Germany and France and this will be fulfilled!

title: Words to the friends, spoken on board the SS Cedric at sea, 1912-Apr-01
first_line: Those who have provided the means for transporting arms and ammunition and the instruments of wars and massacres on earth will do so in the air.
first_line_orig: آنچه در زمین اسباب حمل و نقل آلات و اسباب حرب و قتال ساخته اند در هوا نیز چنان خواهند

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 on 1913-Mar-19
first_line: We must try to return very soon to Haifa. There upon the mountain all alone, pray and supplicate with God. There one finds the ecstasy of spiritual bliss. Supplication, invocation, prayer, inspiration.

title: Words spoken at Hotel Marquardt in Stuttgart, 1913-Apr-04
first_line: I was most happy to see the believers of Germany so holy, so pure and so united

title: Words spoken on 1915-Apr-18 in Haifa
first_line: The House of Justice possesseth legislative authority, and that which hath not been expressly revealed may be legislated by it, and is not revocable. Elections shall be held in diverse provinces, and the House of Justice shall be established, and they shall determine the center thereof according to their own wisdom [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بیت العدل مقام تشریع دارد و آنچه منصوص نیست تشریع نماید و تنفیذی نیست .  در ایالات مختلفه انتخابات می شود و بیت عدل تشکیل شود و مرکز را بصلاح دید خود معین خواهند کرد

title: Grace spoken at Hearst estate in Pleasanton, CA, 1912-Oct-14
first_line: Thou seest us, O my God, gathered around this table, praising Thy bounty, with our gaze set upon Thy Kingdom.
first_line_orig: ترانا یا الهی مجتمعین علی هذه المائدة شاکرین لنعمتک ناظرین الی ملکوتک

title: Words spoken in the presence of Zia Baghdadi, ca. 1920
first_line: The Blessed Beauty often remarked: 'There are four qualities which I love to see manifested in people: first, enthusiasm and courage
first_line_orig: جمال مبارک از چهار چیز خوششان میآید

title: Words to the friends spoken in Dec. 1907
first_line: The Blessed Beauty has provided the means for the unification of the world of humanity and has removed religious and social conflicts.
first_line_orig: جمال مبارک بساط وحدت عالم انسانی گسترانیده و اختلافات مذهبی و طبقاتی را مرتفع ساخته

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken at 309 W 78th St on 1912-Jun-10
first_line: The Blessed Beauty did not make any more public speeches after leaving Baghdad and Adrianople
first_line_orig: جمال مبارک بعد از دارالسلام و ادرنه در محفل عمومی نطق نفرمودند

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-23 in Paris
first_line: All the inhabitants of this city are immersed in this world, and its buildings resemble the hives of bees
first_line_orig: جمیع این اهالی غرق دنیا هستند و عمارات شهر مثل خانه‌های زنبور و مردم متصل مشغول ساختن

title: Answer to questions, Dublin, 1912-Aug-08
first_line: All realities and spirits are immortal, even the spirits of non-believers and imperfect persons.
first_line_orig: جمیع حقایق و ارواح باقیست حتی ارواح غیر مومنین و نفوس ناقصه اما نسبت بارواح

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-12 in London
first_line: In this Cause, all humanity is regarded as a single family, and the whole earth accounted as one country
first_line_orig: در این امر جمعیّت بشر یک عائله و کرّهٴ ارض یکوطن است

title: Words spoken ca. Feb. 1920
first_line: Now if the beloved ones of God would act in accordance with that first tradition, namely, one of the Tablets of the Ancient Beauty, may His glory be exalted [3.5s]
first_line_orig: حالا اگر احبای الهی بهمان حدیث اول یعنی به یکی از الواح جمال قدم جل جلاله عامل باشند

title: Words spoken ca. 1904, from notes of Youness Khan Afroukhteh
first_line: The truth is that it is not befitting for man to be carnivorous. However, man has accustomed himself to such a life
first_line_orig: حقیقتش این است که خوردن حیوانی شایسته نیست اما انسان خود را بی جهت مبتلی کرده و عادی

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-15 in London
first_line: What conspicuous glory has God deigned to bestow upon us Persians! How great is this prosperity, which is even as a mighty sun
first_line_orig: خدا چه عزتی بما ایرانیان عنایت فرمود چه آفتاب بزرگی و سعادتی از افق مشرق زمین طالع

title: Words spoken on the subway on 1912-Jul-06
first_line: In man's nature there must be a desire to ascend and not to descend. The underground air is suffocating.
first_line_orig: در طبیعت انسان باید طلب صعود باشد نه نزول هوای زیر زمین حبس است رفتن از راه بالا بهتر بود

title: Words to the editor of the Police Journal, spoken on 1912-Sep-17
first_line: A newspaper must in the first instance be the means of creating harmony among the people.
first_line_orig: روزنامه باید اول وسیلهٴ الفت بین نفوس باشد این اعظم وظائف صاحبان جرائد است که سوء تفاهم

title: Words spoken on 1914-Dec-16 in Julis
first_line: Visions are of three kinds: true visions, interpretive visions, and confused dreams. The first is reality itself, the second, being mingled with the heart's promptings, requireth interpretation, while confused dreams are but vain imaginings [3.5s]
first_line_orig: رؤیا بر سه قسم است رؤیای صادقه، رؤیای تعبیریه و اضغاث و احلام.  اول عین واقع، دوم چون مخلوط با خطورات قلبیه می شود محتاج تعبیر است، اما اضغاث و احلام اوهام است

title: Words spoken on 1912-Sep-22 in Lincoln
first_line: Shu'a of darkness wrote to his father quite openly that his purpose was to amass wealth and worldly property
first_line_orig: شعاع ظلمانی بالصراحه بپدرش نوشته که من در صدد تحصیل پول و متاع دنیوی هستم

title: Words to Mr Maxwell and others, spoken on 1912-Sep-06
first_line: You must cling to those things which prove to be the cause of happiness for the world of man. You must show kindness to the orphans
first_line_orig: شماها باید بآنچه سبب آسایش عالم انسانی است تشبث نمائید یتیمها را نوازش کنید گرسنه ها را سیر نمائید

title: Words spoken on 1913-Oct-16 in Ramleh
first_line: The Chinese civilization is very old, and hoary with age. Once they start on the right path, they will reach their destination very quickly.

title: Words to some Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Sep-04
first_line: The greatness of the teachings of Baha'u'llah will be known when they are acted upon and practiced.
first_line_orig: عظمت تعالیم حضرت بهآءالله وقتی معلوم می شود که بموقع عمل و اجرا آید هنوز از صد یکی اجرا نشده

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-20 in London
first_line: Do not cry or lament! Do not wail or let tears rain from your eyes! The happiness and sorrow of this world last only for a time, and its glory and abasement are both fleeting
first_line_orig: گریه مکن مویه منما فریاد بر میار اشک از دیده مبار سُرور و حُزن دنیا هر دو در گذر است و عزت و ذلت آن هر دو فانی

title: Words spoken on 1912-Aug-20 in Green Acre
first_line: While the Manifestations of God are still alive, the people do not appreciate their value, they curse and execrate them; but after their ascension they worship them.
first_line_orig: مادام مظاهر الهیه بین خلق هستند و مثل این خیمه نشنینان بیرون گرین عکا شیدا میشود حتی کلمبوس

title: Words spoken on 1915-Jul-21 in Haifa
first_line: The people prostrated themselves before the stones whereon the apostles had been seated, and this proceedeth from their connection with God and from the potency of their enduring reality, such that even their mere act of sitting upon a stone hath produced such an effect [3.5s]
first_line_orig: مردم بر سنگهائی که حواریین برآن  نشسته بودند سجده می کردند و این از اثر نسبت الی الله و از قوهٴ بقای حقیقت آنها است که حتی جلوسشان بر سنگ این تأثیر را دارد

title: Words to some friends, spoken on 1914-Dec-01
first_line: From the age of 30 I have had a slow pulse. All others have a pulse rate of about 75 to 80 and therefore greatly wonder about my pulse rate.
first_line_orig: من از سن سی سالگی نبضم مطئی است هر کس دیگر باشد ٧٥ - ٨٠ خواهد بود

title: Words to Mr Newman, spoken on 1914-Jun-10
first_line: I pray that God may aid your journeys and that you may return to America with the utmost happiness and safety.

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-May-30
first_line: I am the interpreter of the Writings of the Blessed Beauty, as explicitly designated by the Supreme Pen.
first_line_orig: من مبین آیات جمال مبارکم و منصوص قلم اعلی کل باید اطاعت نمایند جمیع امور

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken on 1912-Jun-23
first_line: It is not the place that should be looked at but the illumined faces and hearts of the friends
first_line_orig: نظر بمکان نیست بلکه بوجود و قلوب نورانیه احباست در بغداد اطاقی کوچک ثلث این اطاق بود

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken at Kinney home on 1912-Nov-14
first_line: Singing and chanting of scripture and prayers in verse or in prose should be used but I do not interfere in matters not expressly stated in the Text.
first_line_orig: نغمات و اصوات در تلاوت آیات و مناجات نظم و نهر باید باشد ولی در امور غیر منصوص من مداخله نمیکنم

title: Words spoken at Hearst estate in Pleasanton, CA, 1912-Oct-13
first_line: Every universal matter is from God; and limitations are from man.
first_line_orig: هر امر عمومی الهی است و هر امر خصوصی بشری لهذا خدمات و زحمات نفوس اگر مفید بحال عموم

title: Words spoken at 309 W 78th St in New York, 1912-Jul-11
first_line: Although women are equal to men in abilities and capacities, there is no doubt that men are bolder and physically more powerful
first_line_orig: هر چند نسآء با رجال در استعداد قواء شریکند ولی شبهه نیست که رجال اقدمند و اقوی حتی در حیوانات مانند کبوتران

title: Public address given on 1912-Aug-08
first_line: The more material education advances, the more competitive is the race in aggression and injustice. But spiritual education is the cause of competition in praiseworthy actions
first_line_orig: هر چه تربیت ظاهری بیشتر شود مسابقهٴ در تعدیات زیادتر می شود اما تربیت روحانی سبب مسابقهٴ در اعمال خیریه و کمالات انسانیه است امیدواریم که ازین تعدیات کاسته و روز بروز بر کمالات روحانیه افزوده شود

title: Words to the Master's entourage, spoken on 1912-May-13
first_line: Although I say always that I am ‘Abdu'l-Baha, a servant of God, still people refer to me as a messenger and a prophet. It would be better if they would not attribute such titles to me.
first_line_orig: هر چه ما میگوئیم بندهٴخد‌ا عبدالبها هستیم باز مردم ما را باسم پیغمبر

title: Words to the Baha'is, spoken at Goodall home on 1912-Oct-24
first_line: Every day confirmations surround some specific pursuit and every hour has a purpose decreed for it. Today, teaching the Cause of God
first_line_orig: هر روزی امری مؤید است و هر وقتی مقصدی مقتضی امروز تبلیغ امر الله و نشر تعالیم الهیه جاذب تأییدات غیبیه است وقت تخم افشانیست و القآء کلمهٴ الهی

title: Words to a Rabbi, spoken on 1912-Nov-09
first_line: Whenever these people mention each other's leaders with due reverence then all sufferings and contentions shall cease
first_line_orig: هر گاه این امم رؤسای یکدیگر را به عزت یاد نمایند جمیع ذلتها و جدالها از میان برخیزد بجای نفرت الفت و بجای عداوت و بیگانگی محب و یگانگی حاصل شود مقصد من اینست

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-12 in London
first_line: To the extent that all the Baha'is of the East are ready to give up their lives in their efforts to promote peace. Twenty thousand souls have sacrificed themselves
first_line_orig: بدرجهئ‌یکه جمیع بهائیان شرق بجهت ترویج صلح جان میدهند بیست هزار نفر خود را فدای امر صلح

title: Words spoken in Sep. 1911 in London
first_line: By putting the teaching into practice power will be given. You know which path to follow

first_line: No one can imagine how many different issues must be met….I am now advanced in age. The reaction of this long journey has had a terrible effect upon my weakened constitution…

title: Words spoken on 1914-Jan-27
first_line: We were commanded by Baha'o'llah to assist all the communities without the exclusion

first_line: In an Arabic poem the Blessed Perfection said about the calamities and allegations

first_line: The best capital and the most profitable business is honesty in all things. Do thou continue to be honest in thy dealings

title: Words to Mr McCarthy, spoken on 1912-Oct-06
first_line: I am the lover of all the friends of God -- from the heart and soul I love them. This will become manifest.

title: Words spoken to Miss St. in Aug 1910
first_line: Die richtigen, wahren Bahá'i sind die Schauenden, die Erkennenden, die Wissenden; ihre vornehmste Aufgabe ist, daß sie von der Gnade der Erkenntnis

first_line: When a person's life is purely moral, when his daily actions are propelled by ethical forces he will influence

first_line: The Mashriqu'l-Adhkar must have nine sides, doors, fountains, paths, gateways, columns and gardens

first_line: it is necessary for the rich to think of the poor during the month of Ramadan. Such was the conduct and the life of Baha-Ullah.

first_line: There is but one power which heals -- that is God. The state or condition through which the healing takes

title: Words spoken at Higher Thought center, ca. 1911-Oct-04
first_line: ...it matters not what name each calls himself -- The Great Work is One. Christ is ever in the world of existence

title: Words spoken on 1913-Aug-24 in Ramleh
first_line: As regards free will. There are two distinct kinds of affairs, the first dominated by man, the second which is beyond his control

title: Words spoken at Hotel Ansonia in New York, 1912-Apr-18
first_line: Assuredly, give to the poor. If you give them only words, when they put their hands into their pockets after you have gone, they will find themselves none the richer for you!

title: Words spoken to Miss St. in Aug 1910
first_line: lm Diesseits und Jenseits haben wir Bahá'I nur ein Ziel: für das Reich Gottes (Malekut-Allah) zu leben und zu wirken

title: Words spoken to Miss St. in Aug 1910
first_line: Gottes Führung will uns von der Willkür unserer Sínnlichkeit, von der tollen Eigenmächtigkeit unseres Willens, von der Last unseres kleingläubigen Sorgengeistes

title: Words spoken to Miss St. in Aug 1910

title: Words spoken in the pilgrim house
first_line: One will find it most strange when he reflects on where this Cause once was and where it has now reached. Consider the cities of Shiraz and Tehran
first_line_orig: خیلی عجیب است این امر از کجا بود و بکجا رسید شیراز کجا طهران کجا بغداد کجا رومیبی کجا عکّا و حیفا کجا

title: Words spoken on 1913-Apr-13 in Budapest
first_line: If the inability of a thing which occupies a lower rank of existence to perceive that which occupies a higher rank was itself indicative of the [non-]existence of that higher rank
first_line_orig: عدم احساس و وجدان عالم مادون اگر دلیل بر وجود عالم مافوق باشد نزدیک حیوان جمیع مراتب عقول

title: Words to Mr Schweizer, spoken at Hotel Marquardt on 1913-Apr-29 in Stuttgart
first_line: In you I see such ability that if you should arise to teach the Cause… The Revelation of Baha'u'llah is for action; peruse The Hidden Words and see what He has said therein
first_line_orig: من در تو استعدادی می‌بینم که اگر قیام بر تبلیغ امر کنی چنان تأییدی یابی

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-08 in Paris
first_line: God is the sustainer and the protector of the orphans. How many are the children of the wealthy who went on to wander this world as lost souls
first_line_orig: خدا معین و حافظ ایتام است چه بسیار اطفال اغنیا که در دنیا آواره شدند

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-09 in Paris
first_line: When you turn towards the Abha Kingdom and arise to serve the Cause of God, you will be granted a fresh confirmation day after day
first_line_orig: چون توجّه بملکوت ابهی نمائید و بر خدمت امراللّٰه بر خیزید هر روز تأییدی جدید یابید

title: Words to Mirza Habibu'llah Afnan in 1896-1897
first_line: Recently, a Commission of Inquiry has arrived from Istanbul. Each day, I go to the government office and they interrogate Me

title: Words to Mr Schweizer, spoken at Hotel Marquardt on 1913-Apr-29 in Stuttgart
first_line: I love him [Mirza Abu'l-Fadl] very much. In order to leave himself free to serve the Cause of God, he has not married
first_line_orig: من او را خیلی دوست میدارم این شخص بجهت اینکه در خدمت امر اللّٰه آزاد باشد تأهل ننمود

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-19 in London
first_line: Women must educate themselves and strive to acquire virtues. Moreover, they must win their rights through education
first_line_orig: باید نساء در تربیت خود و تحصیل کمالات بکوشند بتربیت احقاق حقوق خویش نمایند

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-25 in London
first_line: Yesterday, the editor-in-chief of the Christian Commonwealth requested that I write something for publication in his newspaper
first_line_orig: دیروز نظر بخواهش مدیر جریدهٴ کرسچن کامن ولت من برای آن روزنامه چیزی نوشتم که بسبب منازعهٴ

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-30 in Paris
first_line: At a time when the Europeans did not yet enjoy this ascendancy and influence, I had written to 'Abdu'l-Hamid, indicating to him what would come to pass
first_line_orig: قبل از تسلّط و نفوذ اروپائیها حتّی بسلطان عبدالحمید نوشتم که چنین خواهد شد

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-02 in Paris
first_line: The protection of the Cause of God and the unity of the people of Baha are dependent on firmness in the Covenant of God and adherence
first_line_orig: حفظ امر اللّٰه و وحدت اهل بها منوط بثبوت بر عهد اللّٰه است و آثار قلم میثاق مبیّن آیات

title: Words spoken in Ramleh, 1913
first_line: Following the revolution up to the present time, the people of Persia have made repeated attempts to elect people and form consultative assemblies, but the efforts have borne no fruit
first_line_orig: بعد از انقلاب تا حال مکرّر اهل ایران بانتخاب نفوس و تشکیل دارالشّری پرداخته‌اند

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-14 in Liverpool
first_line: After this journey, the call of the unity of humanity and universal peace must be upraised in the Ottoman territories. Their turn shall come
first_line_orig: بعد ازین سفر در ممالک عثمانی باید ندای وحدت عالم انسانی و صلح عمومی بلند شود و نوبت آنحُدود خواهد رسید

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-15 in Liverpool
first_line: It is good that this church is open to everyone, and is the cause of fellowship among every sect and creed, inasmuch as whatever is universal is of God, and that which is particular is of humanity
first_line_orig: این خوب است که آزادی عمومی دارد و سبب الفت هر فرقه و ملّتی است زیرا هر امر عمومی الهی است و هر امر خصوصی

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-13 in Paris
first_line: They [the apostles] gathered on top of a mountain, and made a pact whereby they would consent to bear tribulations
first_line_orig: یک اجتماعی در بالای کُوه نمودند و در قبول بلایا و ترک راحت و نشر هدایت همعهد شدند

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-22 in Paris
first_line: They [the American Baha'is] are people of every stripe. There are those pure Baha'is who believe in all the divine religions and subscribe to the truth of Islam
first_line_orig: از هر قبیل هستند نفوسی بهآئی خالصند که مؤمن  بجمیع ادیان و موقن بحقیقت اسلامند کسانی هستند

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-01 in Paris
first_line: This kind of love is the fruit of consummate reason, for the firmer the foundation of reason and knowledge, the greater the heights that the lofty palace of love will reach
first_line_orig: اینگونه عشق از کمال عقل حاصِل گردد لذا هر قدر بنیان و اساس عقل و معرفت متین‌تر باشد

title: Words spoken on board the SS Celtic at sea, 1912-Dec-07
first_line: Since the people of the East have not treated the attendants of this ship well... I shall come to the table… It is possible that the Europeans believe themselves to be superior to us, but we consider all people the servants of God and regard all humanity the same way
first_line_orig: من سر میز خواهم آمد ولی چند روز میخواهم قناعت داشته باشم والّا شرقیها تحکّمی ندارد

title: Words spoken on board the SS Celtic at sea, 1912-Dec-08
first_line: I have taken 4,600 steps.  This is the distance between the city of 'Akka and the Shrine of Baha'u'llah. I wish to practise walking
first_line_orig: چهار هزار و ششصد قدم راه رفتم بطول راه عکّل تا روضهٴ مبارکه میخواهم مشق راه رفتن کنم

first_line: Share your time with God. Spend half of the day in search of livelihood, guaranteeing your material life and dignified appearance, and dedicate the other half in the acquisition of moral virtues and service at the threshold of God
first_line_orig: اوقات خودت را با خدا تقسیم کن نصف روز را در تلاش معاش و تامین زندگی مادی و شئون ظاهری صرف کن

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-14 in Liverpool
first_line: The foundation of these [Azalis] is chaos and confusion.  From this act which their very leader committed, one can discern the conduct of the others in their ranks
first_line_orig: اساس اینها بر هرج و مرجست از این عمل رئیس اعمال باقی را بفهمید

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-20 in London
first_line: Since we discerned no fruit from the counsel we gave our countrymen, nor could we find a hearing ear among them, we felt it necessary to turn our attention to the West
first_line_orig: چون از نصیحت بهموطنان نتیجهئ‌ی ندیدیم و گوش شنوائی نجستیم لابد توجّه بغرب نمودیم

title: Words spoken on 1913-01-12 in London
first_line: It is not permissible even to strike an animal. When an animal is trained properly, it becomes domesticated
first_line_orig: ضرب برای حیوان هم جائز نه حُسن تربیت حیوان را در تحت تعلیم
subjects: @kindness to and rights of animals, @education of children; moral education, @spiritual transformation

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jan-22 in London
first_line: Instruct the friends to read and disseminate these Tablets. How impressive are the commentaries which the Muslims of former times wrote concerning these verses: 'The Romans have been defeated…'
first_line_orig: بنویسید این الواح مبارکه را بخوانند و نشر دهند سابق مسلمین در تفسیر آلم غلبت الرّوم

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Feb-14
first_line: Though these newspapers will, if written impartially, inform the people, yet we have written articles in the newspapers of the Kingdom
first_line_orig: هر چند این جرائد اگر بیغرضانه بنویسند سبب آگاهی نفوس است ولی ما مقالاتی در جرائد ملکوت نوشتیم

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-03 at Baltimore Hotel in Paris
first_line: If this is indeed the case, then it is an evidence of supreme power, as it is more difficult for the wealthy and noble to profess religious belief than it is for the poor to do this
first_line_orig: اگر چنین است این اقتدار اعظم است زیرا ایمان اغنیا و بزرگان مشکل تر است از ایمان فقرا کار مشکل نمودن

title: Words directed at Mirza Muhammad 'Ali
first_line: Inform my brother that I am not `Alí, nor is he `Umar. I am much greater than `Alí and he is much lesser than `Umar.
first_line_orig: نه تو آن عمر هستی که امر باین عظمت را بلند کنی و نه من آن علی هستم که از دست تو در نخلستان گریه کنم

title: Words spoken on 1912-Dec-27 in London
first_line: I have come to promote divine civilization. This is a civilization that Baha'u'llah established in the East. It is a civilization that tends to the domain of character
first_line_orig: من آمده‌ام تا مدنیّت الهیّه را ترویج نمایم مدنیّتیکه حضرت بهٓاءاللّٰه در شرق تأسیس فرمود

title: Words spoken at Rue St. Didier 30 in Paris, 1913-Feb-14
first_line: The president of last night's gathering stated that Baha'u'llah was the greatest of God's Manfiestations… Yet, the inhabitants of Paris do not share the spirituality and zeal of the Americans, who are truly something else
first_line_orig: دیشب رئیس مجلس گفت حضرت بهآءاللّٰه اعظم مظاهر الهیّه است و ذکر عظمت امر اللّٰه را نمود

title: Words spoken on 1913-Apr-25 in Stuttgart
first_line: Act in accordance with the teachings of Baha'u'llah. Many are the people who peruse the divine teachings, but promptly forget what they have read when the time comes to act
first_line_orig: بموجب تعالیم بهآءاللّٰه عمل کنید بسیاری تعالیم الٓهیّه را میخوانند امّا در موقع فراموش می‌نمایند

title: Words spoken on 1913-Apr-28 in Stuttgart
first_line: Anything is possible, but Jesus Christ, quoting the words of Isaiah, has said, 'They have eyes, but do not see; they have ears, but do not hear
first_line_orig: هر چیزی ممکن است ولکن حضرت مسیح از بیان اشعیا میفرماید که اینها چشم دارند امّا نمی‌بینند گوش دارند ولی نمیشنوند

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-29 in Paris
first_line: How great the results that would have appeared if these people [who were well-versed in Islamic jurisprudence and doctrine] had practised that kind of hair-splitting on matters of actual importance!
first_line_orig: اگر آنگونه موشکافیها در مسائل مهمّه می‌نمودند چه قدر نتائج داشت

title: Words spoken on board the Himalaya at sea, 1913-Jun-13
first_line: How poor are they [labourers on ship], and how hard they toil! The presidents of factories and other operations must allocate a share [of the profits] for the workers in their companies
first_line_orig: چه قدر فقیرند و چگونه زحمت میکشند رؤسای اداره‌ها و کارخانه‌جات باید بجهت مزدوران در کمپانیها

title: Words spoken on board the Himalaya at sea, 1913-Jun-15
first_line: These teachings are what the world needs in this luminous age, for this is not an age of blind imitation; it is the age of light, and the century in which mysteries will be made manifest
first_line_orig: چنین تعالیممایحتاج عالم انسانی در این عصر نورانیست زیرا این عصر عصر تقالید نیست عصر انوار است

title: Words spoken on 1913-Jun-23 in Port Said
first_line: Thoughts of wealth and riches, as well as hopes of rank and glory, are sheer illusion. God has cast these thoughts into our minds only so that this world might prosper; apart from this, they are of no importance
first_line_orig: افکار مال و منال و آمال جاه و جلال صرف اوهام است خدا محض عمران دنیا این اوهام را در سرها انداخته

first_line: Religion and science are as two concentric circles that revolve around one common point, which is reality
first_line_orig: دین و علم دو دائره است که به مرکز واحد سیر میکنند و ان مرکز حقیقت است

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-24 in Paris
first_line: The wisdom of my sojourn here in Paris, as well as the results it will yield, consist in the admonitions I have imparted to the people of the East
first_line_orig: حکمت و نتیجهٴ اقامت در پاریس برای تذکّر مشرقیان و آگاهی ایرانیان بیش از اهالی خود پاریس است

title: Words spoken on 1913-Mar-12 in Paris
first_line: During Baha'u'llah's seclusion in Sulaymaniyyih, He mostly drank milk and ate bread with rice pudding; this is truly excellent sustenance
first_line_orig: در زمان غیبوبت در سلیمانیّه اغلب اوقات شیر میل میفرمودند و نان و شیر برنج فی الحقیقه خوب غذائی است

title: Words spoken at Grand Hotel in Vienna, 1913-Apr-23
first_line: Enter into the Cause of Baha'u'llah and act in accordance with His counsels. When you have attained to the pinnacle
first_line_orig: در امر بهآءاللّٰه داخل شوید و بموجب وصایایش عمل کنید چون در امر بهآءاللّٰه کامل گردید

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-20 in Paris
first_line: There is no state like the state of prayer. It attracts the pure hearts, awakens the holy souls, and confers remarkable spirituality
first_line_orig: هیچ حالتی مثل حالت مناجات نیست قلوب صافیه را منجذب نماید و نفوس مقدّسه را انتباه و روحانیّت عجیبی بخشد

title: Words spoken on 1913-May-31 in Paris
first_line: In the Kingdom of God, women and men are one and the same. It is incumbent on everyone to summon humanity to turn towards the Most Exalted Horizon and to spread the sweet savours of God
first_line_orig: در ملکوت الهی زن و مرد یکسانند جمیع باید ندا بافق اعلی نمایند و نشر نفحات اللّٰه کنند

first_line: The appearance of Rumi and his book, the Masnavi, was like unto a column erected to buttress a tilting wall, enabling the dispensation of Islam to extend twelve hundred years
first_line_orig: ظهور مولوی وکتاب مثنوی مثل شمعی (ستونی) بودکه به زیرآن دیوارمتمایل نصب شد ودوره دیانت اسلام به ١٢٠٠ سال بالغ گردید

title: Words spoken on 1913-Feb-19 in Paris
first_line: It would now be fitting to prepare the means of travel to other planets!
first_line_orig: حال خوب است اسباب مسافرت بکُرات دیگر فراهم کنند

title: Words spoken on 1913-Apr-06 to a minister of Stuttgart
first_line: Do not write to the emperor; he is proud and preoccupied, and will not take heed at present
first_line_orig: امّا بامپراطور آلمان منویس زیرا مغرورند و مشغول حالا گوش نمیدهند

title: Words spoken at Grand Hotel in Vienna, 1913-Apr-23
first_line: The thirsty one must run after the water; the fountain will not run after those who are thirsty

title: Words transcribed on 1915-Dec-19
first_line: I call out in prayer and seek relief for humanity, yet people themselves become the cause of constriction, like [3.5s]
first_line_orig: من دعا میکنم و از برای خلق گشایش می طلبم اما خلق خودشان سبب تنگی میشوند مثل

first_line: Iran requireth divine confirmations, and I hope that just as other countries [have received these] from the Iranians [3.5s]
first_line_orig: ایران تاییدات غیبیه میخواهد امیدوارم همان نوعیکه ممالک سائره از ایرانیان

first_line: Every Manifestation is the Adam of His time... There were one hundred thousand Adams before the Adam of biblical records each being the Manifestation of his own time or cycle.
subjects: @progressive revelation; renewal of religion, @the Adamic cycle and the Baha'i cycle, @Adam; Adam and Eve, @oneness or innumerability of the Manifestations of God, @duration of the Baha'i cycle; future divine revelations, @station of the Manifestation of God

title: Words to John D. Barry
first_line: Society is like the army. There must be degrees. There must be officers and there must be soldiers.

title: Words to John D. Barry spoken at 1815 California Street, 1912-Oct-13
first_line: Our movement goes back to the young leader who called himself The Gate or The Door, in our language, The Báb… The two never met. But at the age of thirty-two Bahá’u’lláh received a tablet from Báb… The first thing he did was to write an epistle to all the kings of the earth and to the pope and to your President

title: Recollections of Juliet Thompson, 1911-Aug-25
first_line: Did you ever think, Juliet, that you and Laura would be riding in an automobile with Me in Europe?

title: Words to Anise Rideout
first_line: The first thing to do is to acquire a thirst for Spirituality, then live the life! Live the life! Live the life!
first_line_orig: اولين قدم ايجاد طلب ورحانيت در قلب است و بعد دارا شدن حيات بهائى حيات بهائى

title: Words spoken on 1915-Nov-10
first_line_orig: باید بشئٍ جزئٍ قناعت نمود و در خدمت عتبه مباركه و نشر نفحات الله جهد و سعى كرد

title: Interview with Kate Carew, Hotel Ansonia and Bowery Mission, on 1912-Apr-19
first_line: The great need of this country is the spiritual philosophy, the philosophy of the language of God. Every one wants to find scientific truths, but we should seek the scientific truths of the spirit as well

title: Address at Oxford University, Manchester College, 1912-Dec-31
first_line: This is indeed a blessed gathering, in the centre of science and learning. In the world of existence today the greatest achievements of man have been made possible through the scientific uncovering of realities.
first_line_orig: لا يكاد الانسان ان يطلع بالسر المكنون فى غيب الامكان الا بعد الخوض

title: Bayan-i-Farsi (Persian Bayan)
first_line: All praise and glory befitteth the sacred and glorious court of the sovereign Lord, Who from everlasting hath dwelt, and unto everlasting will continue to dwell within the mystery of His Own divine Essence… Thou knowest full well, O my God, that tribulations have showered... There is no paradise more wondrous for any soul
first_line_orig: تسبیح و تقدیس بساط قدس عز مجد سلطانی را لایق که لم یزل و لا یزال بوجود کینونیت ذات خود بوده

first_line: Praise be to God, Who hath revealed the verses in truth unto His servant, that perchance mankind might believe in the signs of their Lord. He is assuredly the True One within the heavens and the earth.

first_line: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! first_line: All praise be to God Who hath testified through His Own Self unto His Self that there is none other God but Him, Who hath ascended through the sovereignty of His Being above all things, and Who, through the loftiness of His Revelation, hath concealed Himself from all things - He Who hath everlastingly been, and existed ere the mention of aught else [3.5s]... ...The fifth station testifieth unto God in the mirror of the Letter Há’, and it is the Word that consisteth of the Twin Alifs
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی شهد بذاته لذاته ان لا اله الا هو الذی قد علا بعلو نفسه علی کل شیء و استتر من علو ظهوره عن کل شیء الذی کان لم یزل کان بلا ذکر شیئ

title: Summary of the Kitab-i-Asma'
first_line: Bear thou witness that within that Book, concerning the knowledge of the names of God, exalted and glorified be He, there is inscribed a number corresponding to all things, wherein each one is equated with one in number [3.5s]... ...In the Name of God, the victor of the most victorious, proclaim: God will assist all those who arise to serve Him. No one is able to deprive Him of His majesty, His dominion, His sovereignty, for in the heaven and the earth and in all the realms of God He is the victorious and the conqueror!
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. فاشهد ان فی ذلک الکتاب فی معرفة اسماء الله عز و جل علی عدد کل شیء حیث یعدل واحد فی واحد بالعدد

title: Sahifiy-i-'Adliyya = Risaliy-i-'Adliyyih (Epistle of Justice: Root Principles)
first_line: Praise and thanksgiving befit that Essential Beauty Who hath been from time immemorial single and alone, with naught existing alongside Him, and Who everlastingly endureth in His own Being [3.5s]... ...The supporters of the “oneness of existence” have joined partners with God through their testimony of existence… Since the Ancient of Days created mankind for the purpose of apprehending the power shining within themselves
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. حمد و سپاس وصف جمال ذاتی است که لم یزل بوده یگانه فرد بدون وجود شیئ با او و لایزال بکینونیة خود

title: Sahifiy-i-Makhzunih (Hidden Treasured Epistle)
first_line: Praise be to God Who existed ere all things were brought into being, and with Whom nothing can be compared. He was manifest when there was none other to contemplate His reality. He is the One Whose essence the hearts of the knowing have longed to fathom, yet fail utterly to apprehend even the most infinitesimal glimpse of His attributes [4o]... …The glory of glories and the most resplendent light rest upon Thee, O my God. Thy majesty is so transcendent… O my God, my Lord and my Master! I have detached myself… I adjure Thee by Thy might, O my God!... O My God, O my Lord, O my Master! I beg Thee to forgive me
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی هو کائن قبل کل شیء و لا یکون شیء معه و کان موجوداً حین لا وجود لشیء لدیه الذی قد قصدت افئده العارفین عن معرفة ادنی وصفه

first_line: Verily I am God, no God is there but Me, and aught except Me is but My creation. Say, worship Me then, O ye, My creatures.
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. اننی انا الله لا اله الا انا و ان ما دونی خلقی قل ان یا خلقی ایای فاعبدون قد خلقتک و رزقتک و امتک و احببتک و بعثتک و جعلتک مظهر نفسی لتتلون من عندی ایاتی و لتدعون کل من خلقته الی دینی هذا صراط عز منیع و خلقت کل شیء

title: Tafsir al-Ha I (Tafsir-i-Alifayn: Commentary on the Letter Ha')
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath made the ornament of the Tablets of creation to be the ornament of the Alif standing between two letters, which hath shone forth and gleamed resplendent through that which was cleft asunder and made to speak. Glorified be the Lord of the Throne above whatsoever they who speak may describe, and verily He transcendeth all that they who know can comprehend [3.5s]... ...God, verily, created the Will from nothing through itself… That which I set forth in explanation of the letter Há was to extol the Tree of Bahá, for the supporters of fate recognize the decree of spontaneity
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی جعل طراز الالواح الابداع طراز الالف القائم بین الحرفین الذی لاح و اشرق بما استشقق و استنطق فسبحان رب العرش عما یصف القائلون و انه هو فوق ما یعرف العارفون ...

title: Tafsir (huruf) al-basmala
first_line: Verily God, glorified be He, hath ordained for His Manifestation unto His creation, through His creation, four stations which have been indicated and symbolized [3.5s]... ...The "E" (nún) in the stage of utterance is the same as the "B" (káf). It is the totality of the possible
first_line_orig: بسم الله البدیع الذی لا اله الا هو. ان الله سبحانه قد جعل لظهوره لخلقه بخلقه اربع مقامات المشار الیها والرموز عنها

title: Treatise on the four pillars
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath guided us to the Red Elixir, the foremost habitation raised for humankind in the realm of the heart, set upon the Crimson Dune [4o]
first_line_orig: هو العالی العلی الاعلى بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وبه نستعين. الحمد لله الذی هدانا الی الاکسیر الأحمر و هو اول بیت وضع للناس فی عالم الفؤاد فی کثیب الأحمر
subjects: @language and the structure of reality, @four pillars, @alchemy; the elixir, @progressive revelation; renewal of religion, @spiritual transformation, @multiple meanings; interpretations in scripture, @symbolism

title: Du'a' li-Huruf-i-Bismi'llahi'r-Rahmani'r-Rahim
first_line: Glorified art Thou, O my God! Verily Thou art the Maker of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, their Ordainer, their Fashioner, their Originator and their Author. From time immemorial Thou hast been one God, single, unique, eternal, ever-living and self-subsisting [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. سبحانک اللهم انک انت فاطر السموات و الارض و ما بینهما و مقدرهما و مصورهما و مبدعهما و منشئهما لم تزل کنت الهاً واحداً احداً فرداً صمداً حیاً قیوماً

title: Sahifiy-i-A'mal al-Sanna (Epistle on the Devotional Acts of the Year)
first_line: Praised be to God Who hath, in very truth sent down the Book, a guidance and a remembrance for such as fear God. It is indeed a Book which sets forth regulations pertaining to the month(s) of God in the Qur'an
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی نزل الکتاب بالحق هدی و ذکری للخاشعین و انه لکتاب قد فصل فی حکم شهرالله فی القران هدی و رحمة من عندالله لقوم ساجدین
subjects: @the Imamate; the Caliphate, @spiritual prerequisites of teaching the Cause, @transcendence; unknowability of God, @martyrs and martyrdom, @law of obligatory prayer

title: Javab-i-Ahadin mina's-sabirin
first_line: Praise be to God, who hath brought into being the contingent beings for the purpose of their acceptance, and hath fashioned them in the form of their obedience. Thereupon, He hath raised them up in the stations of command and prohibition, that He might recompense them according to their true deserts. Thereafter, He hath subjected them to trials, that He might distinguish them. Exalted be He! How wondrous is His trial, and how mighty His proof [4o]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی خلق الممکنات لشأن قبولهم و صورهم علی هیکل طاعتهم ثم قد اقامهم فی مقامات الامر والنهی لیجزیهم وصفهم ثم افتتنهم لیمیزینهم فسبحانه ما اعجب فتنته و اعظم بینته

title: Tafsir-i-Haykali'd-Din
first_line: Praise be to God, the All-Knowing, Lord of the Worlds, and verily all glory be from God upon the first Vahid and upon him who resembleth that Vahid wherein naught can be seen save the first Vahid... How then can the effect be equated with the cause [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله العلیم ذی العلامین. الحمد لله العلیم ذی العلامین و انما البهاء من الله علی الواحد الاول ثم من یشابه ذلک الواحد حیث لا یری فیه الا الواحد الاول ... فکیف یعدل بها والمعلول بالعلة ...

title: Du'a' li-Hurufi Bismillahi'l-Amna'i'il-Aqdas
first_line: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! Thou hast ever dwelt alone in Thy dominion of sanctity and majesty, and wilt evermore remain exalted in the celestial heights of holiness and glory [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. سبحانک اللهم یا الهی لم تزل کنت منفرداً فی ملیک القدس والجلال و لا تزال کنت مرتفعاً فی علو سماء القدس والاجلال

title: Tafsir al-Ha II (Tafsir sirr al-ha) (Commentary on the Mystery of Ha')
first_line: Praise be to God Who, through the sanctity of His Essence, transcendeth the comprehension of the most sublime abstractions of divinity and whatsoever... Praise be to God Who bestoweth grace in the Book upon them that have believed [3.5s]... ...For verily each name hath infinite degrees, and the meaning of each thing that is named pertaineth to its own degree
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی تقدس بقدس کینونیته عن عرفان اعلی مجردات اللاهوت و من یشا... الحمد لله الذی یمن فی الکتاب علی الذین آمنوا
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @The Primal Will; self-generation of the Primal Will, @essential vs. actional attributes of God, @impossibility of true worship of God, @Word of God and human limitations

title: Answer to 24 questions of Mulla Ahmad
first_line: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! I and all things bear witness unto Thee that verily Thou art God, and that there is none other God but Thee, alone, without peer. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, Thine the Glory and the Power, Thine the Might and the Empyrean, Thine the Strength and the Brilliance, Thine the Sovereignty and the human realm. Thou givest life and causest death, then bringest death and givest life, and verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the King Who passeth not away, the Sovereign Who changeth not, the Single One Who vanisheth not... powerful over all things. I testify, and all things testify [3.5s]... ...Should a man be endued with knowledge, and behold Thy [God’s] divine verses revealed during earlier times
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. سبحانک اللهم یا الهی لاشهدنک و کل شیء علی انک انت الله لا اله الا انت وحدک لا شریک لک لک الملک و الملکوت و لک العز و الجبروت و لک القدرة و اللاهوت و لک القوة و الیاقوت و لک السلطنة و الناسوت تحیی و تمیت ثم تمیت و تحیی و انک انت حی لا تموت و ملک لا تزول و سلطان لا تحول و فرد لا تفوت ... علی کلشیء قدیرا لاشهدنک و کلشیء
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @power and sovereignty of God; omnipotence of God, @corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God, @oneness or innumerability of the Manifestations of God, @progressive revelation; renewal of religion, @self-concealment of the Manifestation of God, @spiritual prerequisites of teaching the Cause, @forgiveness; grace; bounty; mercy; compassion of God, @suffering and imprisonment

title: Answer to seven questions
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath caused to shine forth that which hath shone forth, and caused to rise that which hath risen, and made to gleam that which hath gleamed, and made utterance to be the letter of derivation at the beginning of separation [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی استشرق ما اشرق و اطلع ما اطلع و الاح ما الاح و جعل الاستنطاق حرف الاشتقاق فی مبدء الافتراق

title: Tafsir al-Hamd
first_line: Praise be to God, Who is sanctified above the essence of all created things' attributes, exalted beyond mere description by contingent beings, and magnified above mention of the camphor of existences... Indeed thou hast known and made mention of that which thou didst mention concerning the pure Leaf, and what have people to do with partaking of that hidden fruit which her Lord hath reserved for her [3.5s]... ...When it [the Point] appeared there was [also] manifest that which is Unseen, namely, the letter alif
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله المتقدس عن جوهر نعت الموجودات و المتعالی عن مجرد وصف الممکنات و المتکبر عن ذکر کافور اللکینونیات ... قد علمت قد ذکرت ما ذکرت فی ذکر ورقة الطاهرة و ما للناس والاخذ من تلک الثمرة الجنیه قد رکنها ربها لنفسها
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity, @names and attributes of God, @the Word of God; influence and centrality of, @da'iras and haykals, @prayer for tests and difficulties

title: Kitabu'l-Qiyama
first_line: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, and that whatsoever is other than Him is His creation, and all are His worshippers. And verily I bear witness unto God, my Lord, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, Lord of all things [3.5s]
first_line_orig: هو الاقدس. شهد الله أن لا اله الا هو و إن ما دونه خلق له و کل له عابدون  و إنی لأشهدن الله ربی رب السموات و رب الأرض رب کل شیء

title: Kitabu'l-Mulk
first_line: In the name of God, the Sovereign, the Sovereign! In the Name of God, the Sovereign, the Sovereign! In the Name of God, the King of Kings! In the Name of God, the All-Possessing, the All-Possessing [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الاملک الاملک. بسم الله الملک الملک بسم الله الملک الملک بسم الله الملک الملاک بسم الله المالک المالک

title: Lawh-i-Haykalu'd-Din
first_line: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, the King, Possessor of the Kingdoms. In the First Gate He hath ordained mention of His Own Self, His Very Self - verily there is none other God but Him. His are the sovereign Names unto all eternity, like unto eternity. In the Second Gate He hath ordained [3.5s]... ...Ye shall assuredly find All Good in the numerical difference between Qá’im and Qayyúm, in nine years
first_line_orig: هو. شهد الله انه لا اله الا هو الملک ذو الملاکین قد قدر فی الباب الاول ذکر نفسه نفسه انه لا اله الی هو له الاسماء الملکی ... الابد مثل الابد قد قدر فی الباب الثانی

title: Tawqi'i-i-Dhahabiyyih (Risaliy-i-Dhahabiyya II)
first_line: Praise be to God, the One, the Single, the Peerless, the All-Compelling, the Eternally Besought, the Unique, the Ever-Abiding, the Almighty, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Exalted, the All-Choosing, the All-Powerful, the Just, the All-Forgiving, Who through His command hath created the essences of mysteries [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الواحد الاحد الفرد القهار الصمد الوتر الدائم الجبار الحی القیوم المتعال المختار المقتدرالعادل الغفار الذی خلق بامره جوهریات الاسرار

title: Risala fi Tashkhis al-Ghina (on singing)
first_line: Praise be to God Who, through the sanctity of His Essence, hath sanctified Himself above the attributes of essences and all that pertaineth thereunto; and praise be to God Who, in His primal Eternity, hath singled out His oneness above the description of intrinsic qualities and their like [3.5s]... ...The reality of all beings, save God, dependeth on two aspects. The first is the existential aspect (jihat-i-vujúdí) which indicateth the divine effulgence
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی تقدس تقدیس قیومته عن نعت الجوهریات و ما یشاء بهها و الحمد لله الذی تفرد بتفرد ازلیته عن وصف الذاتیات و ما یعادلها
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @martyrs and martyrdom, @the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer

title: Sahifiy-i-Vaviyyih
first_line: Praise be to God, Who judgeth between men in truth concerning that wherein they differ. He it is Who hath sent down the verses [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرب الفعال المختار. الحمد لله الذی یفصل بین الناس بالحق فیما هم فیه یختلفون هو الذی انزل الایات
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @impossibility of true worship of God, @forgiveness; grace; bounty; mercy; compassion of God, @power and sovereignty of God; omnipotence of God, @justice and wrath of God

title: Risala Furu' al-'Adliyya (Epistle of Justice: Branches)
first_line: God hath enjoined upon mankind certain ordinances prior to the act of prayer, and among them is His decree that He imposeth no burden upon any soul beyond its capacity, nor is anyone to be compelled in any matter [4o]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. و لقد فرض الله علی الناس قبل الصلوة بعضاً من الاحکام و هی ان الله لا یکلف لاحد الا دون قوته و ما یجبر علی احد لشیء

title: Kitabu'sh-Shahadah
first_line: Praise and glory befit that Most Sacred Being, Who hath ever been sanctified beyond the description of aught else beside Him [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسمه العلی العظیم. حمد و ثناء ذات اقدسی را سزاوار است که لم یزل منزه بوده طلعت حضرت او از وصف ماسوای او
subjects: @transcendence; unknowability of God, @walking the spiritual path; spiritual wayfaring; the virtuous life, @impossibility of true worship of God, @prayer for firmness in the Covenant

title: Du'a' li-Hadrat-i-Ni'ma
first_line: Glorified art Thou, O my God, and praise be unto Thee! I testify unto Thee at this moment, through my unity with Thee and my confession of Thine eternity and my certitude of Thy oneness, by the essence of the camphor of my reality, the pure manifestation of my being, and the uttermost boundaries of the hidden signs of my identity... Say: He is God, the One! God, the Self-Subsisting! He begetteth not, nor is He begotten, and there is none like unto Him. Yea, verily, Thou art God [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. سبحانک اللهم و بحمدک اشهدک حینئذ بتوحیدی ایاک و اقراری بازلیتک و ایقانی بوحدانیتک بجوهر کافور ذاتیتی و مجرد ظهور کینونیتی و منتهی غایات خفیات انیتی ... قل هو الله احد الله الصمد لم یلد و لم یولد و لم یکن له کفوا احد بلی انک انت الله

title: Risalata'l-Ishraq
first_line: Praise be to God Who hath brought forth the Primal Will before all else, that His divine sovereignty might be made manifest in the kingdom of command and creation, and that all atoms might come to know [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد لله الذی ابدع المشیة قبل کلشیء لظهور قیومیته فی ملکوت الامر و الخلق لیعلم کل الذرات

title: Answer to a letter from Dayyan
first_line: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! I and all things bear witness unto Thee that verily Thou art God, and that there is none other God but Thee, alone, without peer. Thine is the Kingdom and the Dominion, Thine the Glory and the Power, Thine the Strength and the Empyrean, Thine the Might and the Brilliance, Thine the Sovereignty and the human realm, Thine the Glory and the Majesty, Thine the Countenance and the Perfection, Thine the Splendor and the Beauty, Thine the Mercy and the Bounty, Thine the Authority and the Justice, Thine the Symbol and the Similitudes, Thine the Stations and the Reverence, Thine the Power and the Action, Thine the Example and the Exemplars, Thine the Grandeur and the Majesty [3.5s]

title: Kitabu'l-Ba'th
first_line: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him. His is the creation and the command. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. In His grasp is the dominion of all things; He createth whatsoever He willeth by His command, and verily, He hath power over all things. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Me, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved. God beareth witness that there is none other God but God. Say: All, by night and by day, worship Him [3.5s]
first_line_orig: بسم الله الامنع الاقدس. شهد الله انه لا اله الا هو له الخلق و الأمر یحیی و یمیت ثم یمیت و یحیی و انه هو حی لا یموت فی قبضته ملکوت کلشیء یخلق ما یشآء بأمره انه کان علی کل شیء قدیرا شهد الله انه لا اله الا انا العزیز المحبوب شهد الله انه لا اله الا الله قل کل باللیل و النهار له عابدون
